title: Celebrating 2026 Internet Archive Artist in Residence: Christopher Burch
content:
Written by VITA HEWITT

“Echoes of Absence and Mythos: The Un-Archivists of Shitocracy” comes straight from the hands of artist Christopher Burch and opens on October 17 at Incline Gallery. Created in collaboration with the Internet Archive, D. Scott Miller, who wrote the Afro Surrealist Manifesto, and Incline Gallery, with funding from the San Francisco Arts Commission, this exhibition takes aim at the dual specters of societal erasure of Black experience and the often unmet need to amplify marginalized voices.

The Un-Archivists of Shitocracy, an imagined secret society comprised of those overlooked by history, takes these heavy subjects on through historical and contemporary contexts, mixed together with the hands of a trickster to challenge oppressive systems that seek to erase the narratives crucial to Black identity.

title: VISEK-apurahat tulevat hakuun marraskuussa
content:
Visuaalisen alan taiteilijoiden VISEK-apurahat ovat haettavissa marraskuussa. Apurahojen hakuaika on 2.–15.11.2026. Työskentelyapurahoja on jaossa yhteensä 63 000 euroa.

Kuvaston osana toimiva Visuaalisen taiteen edistämiskeskus VISEK myöntää työskentelyapurahoja visuaalisen alan ammattitaiteilijoille ja -taiteilijaryhmille. Apurahojen hakuaika alkaa maanantaina 2. marraskuuta ja päättyy sunnuntaina 15. marraskuuta klo 23.59. Hakuohjeet ja -lomake julkaistaan Kuvaston verkkosivuilla 2.11. klo 9.

Taiteilijoiden taiteelliseen työskentelyyn tarkoitettujen apurahojen suuruus on 3 000 euroa. Apurahoja on jaossa 21 kappaletta, yhteensä 63 000 euroa.

VISEK-apurahat rahoitetaan pääosin opetus- ja kulttuuriministeriön VISEKille osoittamasta yksityisen kopioinnin hyvityksestä. Kuvasto joutui peruuttamaan vuosi sitten apurahahaun hyvitykseen kohdistuneen valtion budjettileikkauksen vuoksi. Nyt hakuun tulevat apurahat katetaan VISEKin vuoden 2025 ja 2026 hyvitysvaroista.

title: Varokaa heikkoa jäänlukutaitoa
content:
”Varokaa heikkoa jäätä, mmm…”, toteaa Pikku Kakkosen nalle möreällä äänellään pudottuaan ensin jäihin Pikku Kakkosen Heikot jäät: Varokaa heikkoa jäätä! -tietoiskussa. Lyhytelokuvaa on esitetty syksyisin ja keväisin vuodesta 1986 alkaen, siis jo neljäkymmentä vuotta. Sen tietyllä tapaa epätodellinen ja lapsen mielestä ehkä myös karmiva äänimaailma yhdistettynä jäiden seassa hätääntyneenä räpiköivään nalleen ovat eittämättä jääneet lukuisten suomalaisten lasten mieliin. Se on varoittanut, että jäille ei kannata noin vain lähteä.

Heikot jäät ja jäihin putoaminen ovat toistuva teema mediassa ja kulttuurissa. Syksyisin vesien alkaessa jäätyä ja keväisin jäiden sulaessa sanomalehdet täyttyvät varoituksista, kuinka jäällä ei ole vielä turvallista liikkua tai kuinka se ei enää ole turvallista. Saaristolaisromaaneissa juuri jäihin hukkuminen nousee usein dramaattiseksi käännekohdaksi. Näin on esimerkiksi Anni Blomqvistin Myrskyluoto-sarjassa (1968–1973) ja Ulla-Lena Lundbergin romaanissa Jää (2012). Omalla kohdallani kaikki tämä oli luonut ajatuksen, että jää on jotakin poikkeuksellisen petollista ja vaarallista. Uskoakseni sama mielikuva on myös monella muulla suomalaisella.

title: Islan metsä on nyt suojeltu: Luonnonperintösäätiö hankki arvokkaan metsäalueen Karstulasta
content:
Luonnonperintösäätiö on ostanut Karstulan Hinkalon entisen leirikeskuksen läheltä reilun kuuden hehtaarin metsäalueen pysyvään suojeluun. Alue hankittiin Saarijärven seurakunnalta Islan metsä -kampanjassa kerättyjen lahjoitusvarojen turvin.

Karstulan Pääjärven itäpuolella sijaitseva suojelukohde rajautuu suoraan yli 16 hehtaarin Hinkalon luonnonsuojelualueeseen ja kasvattaa alueen ympärille muodostuvaa yhtenäistä suojelumetsien kokonaisuutta.

Islan metsän alueella kasvaa varttunutta, osittain jo vanhaa mänty- ja kuusimetsää. Erityisen arvokas on noin hehtaarin laajuinen luonnonmetsämäinen vanha männikkö, jossa esiintyy eri-ikäistä puustoa sekä järeitä haapoja. Inventoinneissa alueelta on havaittu muun muassa teeri, hömötiainen ja töyhtötiainen.

Alueen suojeluarvoa lisää sijainti olemassa olevan luonnonsuojelualueen yhteydessä. Näin Hinkalon alueen suojelumetsäkokonaisuus kasvaa ja tarjoaa aiempaa paremmat edellytykset metsälajien elämälle ja säilymiselle luonnossa sekä myös ihmisten virkistymiselle.

title: Sloveniassa on enemmän traktoreita kuin missään muualla, ja Jugoslaviassa varttuneelle Bogdan Pregeljille se tuo vapauden: ”Aiemmin kärsin, koska en voinut tehdä haluamiani asioita”
content:
”Traktori on vapautta”, sanoo slovenialainen Bogdan Pregelj, 47, jonka uutuuttaan hohtava, Fendt-merkkinen traktori seisoo uljaana hänen kotitalonsa viereisessä autotallissa. Olemme Länsi-Sloveniassa, Col-nimisessä kylässä, ja Bogdan on spontaanisti kutsunut pyöräilevän perheemme tienvarresta kotiinsa leveä hymy kasvoillaan.

Talossa on tilaa, sillä sisätiloissa yönsä viettää ainoastaan Pregeljin vaimo Sabina. Pregeljin vanhimmat pojat ovat lomilla, ja nuorin nukkuu sään salliessa mieluummin talon ulkoterassilla kuin omassa sängyssään.

Pregelj itse aikoo suunnata pimeän tullen makuualusta kainalossa metsän keskelle. Siellä uni tulee kuulemma paremmin.

Mutta ensin jutellaan traktorista, jonka Pregelj on hetkeäkään empimättä nimennyt elämänsä tärkeimmäksi esineeksi.

”Aikuisten ja lasten lelujen ero näkyy hintalapussa”, Pregelj naureskelee vihreä-keltaista menopeliä esitellessään. Toisen traktorinsa hiljattain ostanut mies on silminnähden onnellinen.

Kyseisen ”lelun” hintalappu on 250 000 euroa, ja ikää sillä on kolme kuukautta.

Sloveniassa ei ole lainkaan epätavallista, että perheellä on oma traktori, sillä suurin osa maan maa- ja metsäalasta on suuryritysten sijaan yksityisomistuksessa.

title: Osastopäällikkö kansainvälisen kaupan osastolle
content:

title: DarkDes – ett gränssnittsexperiment för arkitektursamlingar
content:
I KOD-brev 14 efterfrågades recensioner av nya DigitaltMuseum (DiMu). Jag har länge frustrerats av deras sökgränssnitt. Under sommarledigheten bestämde jag mig för att koda fram hur jag tyckte att en sök-i-samlingarna egentligen borde se ut.

Resultatet finns på https://darkdes.net/ – en inofficiell söktjänst för ArkDes samlingar. Förhoppningsvis kan detta projekt väcka lite diskussion kring användargränssnittens roll i digital samlingsförvaltning.

Vilka är vi som ligger bakom sajten? Jag är frilansande arkitekt och mjukvaruutvecklare och jobbar med samlingsförvaltning på ArkDes. Jag har samarbetat med min programmerarvän Love Lagerkvist och vi har använt oss av OpenAI:s Sol 5.6 för en stor del av utvecklingsarbetet. Jag vill också passa på att lyfta FOU-projektet Ett nätverk av platser som en viktig inspirationskälla.

Nedan redogör jag för de huvudsakliga designbesluten som lett fram till DarkDes nuvarande gränssnitt, och kontrasterar dem mot DiMu där det är hjälpsamt.

title: NORDIS assesses threats to the Danish information environment
content:
NORDIS partner TjekDet has published a comprehensive written threat assessment of misinformation, disinformation and other developments that may affect the Danish information environment.

Denmark continues to have a strong information environment. But the ways in which misinformation emerges, spreads and affects us are changing constantly and rapidly.

This is the starting point for the Threat Assessment 2026, which brings together the NORDIS and TjekDet’s editorial team’s assessment of the most significant threats to the Danish information environment.

One of the report’s overall conclusions is that Denmark continues to have a fundamentally robust information environment, but also that the threat landscape has become far more complex than it was just five or six years ago.

title: Five Arrested in 1 Million Euro Fraud Against NATO
content:
European authorities arrested five people in Norway and raided properties in Germany and Romania as part of an investigation into a company suspected of defrauding NATO member countries of more than 1 million euros ($1.11 million), Eurojust said Wednesday. The targeted company and its subcontractors allegedly provided shore-based support—known as husbandry services—to NATO military vessels visiting ports in northwestern Europe.

The network is accused of submitting fraudulent invoices and using an intermediary to bribe foreign public officials to secure favorable contracts with the alliance. NATO's procurement agency, the NSPA, discovered the billing anomalies, triggering a cross-border probe in April 2025. Eurojust noted that the exact financial loss is still being calculated by the joint investigation team, which involves anti-corruption police and prosecutors from Norway, Romania, Germany, and the U.K.

title: Why Cleopatra, Lawrence of Arabia, Ben-Hur & Other Hollywood Classics Still Look So Good
content: Cleopatra cost Twentieth Century Fox $44 million, by the studio’s own estimate. That may sound like the budget of one of those genre pictures that winds up going straight to streaming, but if we convert those 1963 dollars into current ones, it comes out to $480 million. The most expensive film ever made up to that point, it remained an industry symbol of near-parodically troubled production and grotesque cost inflation for decades. Like The Wizard of Oz, it failed to recoup its investment during its initial theatrical run, eventually turning a profit thanks only to re-releases and television rights sales. And yet, these six decades later, the investment seems to have proven sound, at least according to the video above from YouTube channel Wolfcrow, “Why Cleopatra Still Looks Like a Trillion Bucks.”

title: These Women Were Trying to Escape Domestic Abuse. ICE Detained Them Instead.
content:
They were victims, not abusers. That’s what they told police officers, attorneys, visitors and anyone else who would listen. It didn’t matter. The women were all taken to a sprawling immigration detention center in the woods of west Michigan and handed thin jumpsuits — red, to mark them as a high security risk.

Inside the North Lake Processing Center, they talked about the men whose calls to police landed them there. The boyfriends or husbands who threatened to get them deported and cut them off from their children. The men, or sometimes women, who hit them, pulled their hair or choked them, bruising their throats.

They didn’t know where to go for help before, but now, in the confines of a cold cellblock in a former prison, the women helped one another. If one spoke to somebody on the outside who could connect them with advice, legal aid or money for the commissary, she’d pass around a tablet used for calls so others could tell their stories.

title: How to watch the EU leaders’ summit like a pro
content:
BRUSSELS — European leaders came for the budget. They’re staying for everything else.

A two-day European Council starting Thursday was supposed to be all about the money. Instead, leaders of the 27 EU member countries are heading into one of their most crowded summits in years, with a succession of geopolitical crises threatening to hijack the EU’s carefully laid plans.

European Council President António Costa originally wanted the gathering to accelerate negotiations on the bloc’s next seven-year budget, hoping to seal a deal before elections in France, Italy and Poland in 2027 make an already difficult agreement even harder.

But the world had other plans. Soaring energy prices, tensions with China, Russia’s war in Ukraine (and U.S. President Donald Trump’s ambiguity over it), migration and turmoil in the Middle East have all elbowed their way onto the agenda.

The result is a two-day marathon covering virtually every major challenge facing the EU, from keeping European factories competitive to ensuring the world’s most important shipping lanes stay open.

For anyone trying to follow the action without spending 48 hours glued to Brussels, here’s your guide to what matters.

title: Ready player one? Why the games arcade is having a rebirth
content:
After years of sprawling ‘forever’ games, players are rediscovering the pleasures of more focused experiences. Could a new wave of independent arcades bring back the social side of gaming?

• Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

There’s an important semi-nostalgic movement happening in games, and I’m excited about where it’s heading. But I don’t want to get ahead of myself here.

Over the last five years, major publishers, obsessed with the success of “forever games” such as Fortnite, Minecraft and Roblox, have been throwing hundreds of millions of dollars into their own sprawling, endlessly updating, battle-pass-infested mega franchises – each designed to take all our time and money. The result has been astounding failures such as Concord, Mindseye and Tales of the Shire. Even the good games – Crimson Desert, Path of Exile 2, Blood of the Dawnwalker – are so bloated they have become the unyielding masters of our precious few hours of free time.

title: Maricarmen Abascal: how a disabled, evicted 87-year-old woman became a political football in Spain’s upcoming election
content:
In Spain, an average of 44 evictions are carried out every day. While statistics like this are shocking, numbers alone rarely spark a revolution. Mass protest movements instead tend to rally around one compelling individual story.

This was exactly what happened with 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal, who has become so famous that she is known in Spain as simply Maricarmen. Following an insurmountable rent hike and a lengthy legal battle, she was evicted from her Madrid home of 71 years in September, and died on October 7. She quickly become a household name, and the figurehead of Spain’s housing protests.

Her case stirred the empathy of millions, and inspired collective shame that society was unable to prevent an elderly woman from being forced out of her home on a stretcher. Her story made headlines around the world, sparked a wave of fierce, nationwide protests, and led to an unravelling of Spanish politics that has culminated in a snap election on November 29 and a general strike planned for November 11.

title: Yemen’s Houthis are bringing their war to Saudi Arabia – and reframing the narrative of being an Iranian proxy
content:
A deadly Houthi attack on Riyadh’s international airport has highlighted how the Yemeni group is reframing its perceived “Iran proxy” role and shifting its regional focus to its ongoing battle against Saudi Arabia. The Oct. 10 strike, in which 13 people were killed and hundreds injured, was the most violent episode on Saudi Arabian soil since the beginning of the war in Iran in February.

It was followed by further – albeit less deadly – missile barrages in the days since. The violence, moreover, comes just as the kingdom is hosting a major conference for oil producers.

As a longtime analyst of Yemeni politics, I see the latest attacks as another illustration of both the expanding regional stalemate across the Middle East and the need to understand how Yemen’s decade-long war is having effects far beyond its territory.

title: Announcing the Publication of an Agentic Assessment Tool for Public Data at Risk
content:
Akshay Mehta is a PhD student in computer science at Boston University and a fellow with the Public Data Project, where he built the website and background agent for the AI Benchmarking Exercise.

Leaders at OpenAI, Nvidia, and IBM have predicted on separate occasions that 2025 would be the year of AI agent adoption. More recently, Microsoft has declared 2026 the year of the agent. Yet as of May 2026, just 19.8% of U.S. businesses reported using AI in any business function, according to the Census Bureau’s Business Trends and Outlook Survey. Still, these systems will be increasingly deployed, raising numerous concerns. Empirical benchmarking of their reliability in domain-specific use cases remains thin, and if we are to take agentic use seriously in research environments, we must close this gap.

As the Public Data Project’s Molly Hardy detailed in an earlier blog post, our team, in partnership with dataindex.us, created an AI benchmarking exercise to test how well AI can assess data risk for federal datasets. We have now built the AI Benchmarking Exercise into a web-based application, and we’re excited to announce its publication!

title: Suomi hyötyy vahvasta EU:n tutkimus- ja innovaatiorahoituksesta – Unifi varoittaa leikkauksista
content:
Unifi peräänkuuluttaa päätöksiä EU:n tutkimus- ja innovaatiorahoituksen vahvistamiseksi. EU-rahoituksen leikkaaminen heikentäisi myös Suomen kilpailukykyä.

Neuvoston tuoreessa EU:n monivuotista rahoituskehystä (MFF) koskevassa neuvotteluesityksessä tulevan Horisontti Eurooppa -ohjelman rahoitusta esitetään leikattavaksi 9,6 prosenttia Euroopan komission alkuperäisestä ehdotuksesta samalla, kun myös muihin kilpailukykyä ja innovaatioita tukeviin ohjelmiin kohdistuu vähennyksiä. Unifi pitää ehdotettuja leikkauksia lyhytnäköisinä tilanteessa, jossa Eurooppa kohtaa kiristyvän kansainvälisen kilpailun tutkimuksessa, teknologiassa ja osaamisessa.

title: How Europe’s most wanted cocaine trafficker turned Sierra Leone into the world’s first true narco state
content:
Drawing on dozens of interviews with intelligence and police officers across two continents, a Guardian investigation reveals the murderous cost of our insatiable appetite for cocaine

Read more: Latin American organised crime ‘may operate in 16 European countries’
Explainer: What is state capture and why does it matter?

As abductions go, few have been more brazen. Alan Jalloh was with two friends outside Goodies supermarket, frantic as usual with late afternoon shoppers. Rush hour in downtown Freetown, Sierra Leone’s capital, was under way with familiar gusto.

A black Toyota Rav4 forced its way through the Peninsula highway traffic. Witnesses describe burly white men leaping out, yanking on balaclavas. Jalloh, 40, seemed to freeze. As did his two friends, one a famous Freetown footballer. All three were dragged into the waiting SUV. None of them have been seen since.

title: ”Kriittisiä raaka-aineita tarvitaan, mutta ei hinnalla millä hyvänsä” – Ohisalo arvostelee komission kaivospäätöksiä
content:
Vihreiden europarlamentaarikko Maria Ohisalo on pettynyt Euroopan komission päätökseen päästää Suomeen uusia kriittisiin raaka-aineisiin liittyviä hankkeita. Viiankiaava on hänen mukaansa yksi varoittava esimerkki näistä myönnöistä.

Komissio nimesi viime perjantaina 46 uutta strategista hanketta kriittisten raaka-aineiden asetuksen nojalla. Viisi hankkeista sijaitsee Suomessa: Sokli, Suhanko, Hautalampi, CoNiKo ja Project Arctial.

Ohisalon mukaan strategisen projektin status tarkoittaa väistämättä ohituskaistaa luvitukseen, ja komissio on kerta toisensa jälkeen myöntänyt sen hankkeille, joissa ympäristövaikutusten arviointi on tekemättä.

Ohisalon mukaan pahin esimerkki on viime vuonna statuksen saanut Sakatin kaivoshanke, joka uhkaa Viiankiaavan ainutlaatuista luontoa.

Uudella kierroksella hän pitää erityisen pöyristyttävänä Itä-Lapin Savukoskella sijaitsevan Soklin nimeämistä. Ohisalon mukaan tämän malminkaivuuhankkeen ympäristö- ja vesiluvat hylättiin korkeimmassa hallinto-oikeudessa merkittävien ympäristöriskien vuoksi, mutta hanke sai silti komissiolta strategisen aseman.

title: Country Perspectives: The Journey of Central America and the Dominican Republic
content: The Journey of Central America and the Dominican Republic in the “Unlocking IP-backed Financing Series” provides an overview of the IP finance landscape across Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama, where legal frameworks generally allow intellectual property assets to be used as collateral but the practical use of IP-backed financing remains at an early stage. The report examines key challenges, including limited market experience, limited familiarity with intangible assets within the financial sector, the limited use of valuation practices, and the need for stronger links between IP, innovation and financial ecosystems. It also highlights growing interest among financial institutions in exploring new financing approaches and identifies actions to strengthen technical capacity, institutional coordination and the gradual integration of IP into financing mechanisms across the region.

title: Saudi Arabia/Yemen: Civilians must not pay the price of escalation in hostilities
content:
Responding to the dramatic escalation of armed hostilities between the Huthi de facto authorities, the Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia in recent weeks and the growing toll on civilians amidst ongoing attacks, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa, Heba Morayef, said:  

“The risks to civilians in Yemen and Saudi Arabia are rapidly increasing each day this conflict escalates. All parties to the conflict must ensure civilians are protected and abide by their obligations under international humanitarian law.  

“Over the past week, deadly Huthi attacks on airports in Saudi Arabia have caused significant civilian harm, including a 10 October attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed 13 people and wounded hundreds more- the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in over a decade. The attack came amidst the return of full-blown armed hostilities to Yemen with devastating consequences for civilians there, particularly on the coast and around Ta’iz, Yemen’s third largest city.  

Civilians are never legitimate targets. They must not pay the price of further escalation.

Heba Morayef, Amnesty International

title: Russia Restocks its Hostage Bank
content:
The main Russian security service, the FSB, arrested a foreign reporter on suspicion of espionage — this time a journalist for the Japanese newspaper Hokkaido Shimbun in the Far Eastern Sakhalin region.

The incident is the latest addition to what some journalists-in-exile refer to as the Kremlin’s exchange fund. Others in the West term it a hostage bank of Westerners visiting Russia who are plucked by the FSB as a means to apply duress on their governments.

Thirty-four-year-old Yuki Imai looked bewildered and shocked as several masked FSB operatives stormed his hotel room in Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, on the Pacific island of Sakhalin in Russia’s Far East, and threw him half-naked onto the floor. The FSB brazenly advertised its visible brutality with a video showing his arrest.

The Japanese journalist was then put on a plane bound for Moscow, and upon landing immediately taken to a Moscow court, which ruled that he should be sent to Lefortovo — the notorious FSB prison — and kept in a cell until December 12.

title: "Bogus": Minnesota State Senator Zaynab Mohamed on DHS Raid on Rep. Ilhan Omar's D.C. Home
content:
On Monday, federal agents from the Department of Homeland Security raided the Washington, D.C., home of Congressmember Ilhan Omar. Omar has faced years of racist targeting from President Trump over her ethnicity and immigrant background. She immigrated to the United States as a refugee from Somalia when she was a child. Omar is the first Somali American elected to federal office, the first woman of color to represent Minnesota and, along with Michigan’s Rashida Tlaib, one of the first Muslim women to serve in Congress.

“Congresswoman Omar has been under attack by this administration for the last decade. … She’s a symbol of everything that this administration hates: an immigrant who stands up for her community, who fought to be here in this country, and now is doing her job and her duty to serve her constituents,” says our guest Zaynab Mohamed, a fellow Somali immigrant who represents Minneapolis in Minnesota’s state Senate. As Trump spews racist invective against the Somali American community in Minnesota, Mohamed says, “We will continue to do everything we can to reject this type of hate and rhetoric from this administration.”

title: The biggest EU sanctions package has been adopted
content:
On 12 October 2026, the Council of the European Union adopted a significant expansion of its restrictive measures against Russia in response to Russia’s continued military aggression against Ukraine, in particular its recent military campaign affecting civilian infrastructure. The new measures represent the largest single addition to the EU’s Russia-related sanctions listings since the beginning of the full-scale invasion in February 2022.

The newly adopted measures expand the EU’s Russia-related sanctions list by 1,569 listings, comprising 826 companies in the military-industrial complex and 743 individuals who serve as their chief executive officers.

title: DHS Inspector General Finds That TSA is Not Properly Safeguarding Passenger Facial Recognition Data
content:
EFF legal intern Gabrielle Ladun was the principal author of this post. 

The Department of Homeland Security Office of Inspector General (DHS OIG) has published a summary of findings from its audit of the Transportation Security Administration’s (TSA) facial recognition technology. While the detailed findings are classified, the summary states that the OIG’s audit uncovered a “significant weakness” in the technology’s ability to protect the privacy of passenger data. This has massive privacy implications for the millions of passengers who travel and don’t opt out of the TSA’s biometric surveillance technology verification process. 

TSA uses facial comparison technology for identity verification of airline passengers. A camera takes a photo of passengers to verify that their provided identification matches their live photo. Although TSA states that it is “committed to protecting traveler privacy,” the audit highlights that this has not been the case.

title: Palkkaero ei kavennu yksin työpaikoilla – ratkaisut löytyvät työurien rakenteista ja hoivavastuun jaosta
content:
Suomessa sukupuolten välisen palkkaeron kaventaminen edellyttää nykyistä vaikuttavampia ja paremmin kohdennettuja toimia. Tuoreen policy briefin mukaan samapalkkaisuustyössä on siirryttävä laajoista toimenpidelistoista tutkimusnäyttöön perustuviin, arvioitaviin toimiin, jotka puuttuvat työurien rakenteisiin, ammattien segregaatioon ja hoivavastuun jakautumiseen.

Suomessa sukupuolten palkkaero on edelleen noin 15 prosenttia, eikä samapalkkaisuusohjelmien vaikutuksia ole kyetty osoittamaan luotettavasti. Laboren ja Etlan tuoreessa policy briefissä Samapalkkaisuustyöstä vaikuttavampaa esitetään, että samapalkkaisuustyön painopiste tulisi siirtää toimenpidelistauksista mitattaviin tuloksiin ja vaikuttaviin interventioihin.

– Suomessa on tehty paljon samapalkkaisuuden eteen, mutta liian usein onnistumista on mitattu toteutuneilla toimenpiteillä eikä niiden vaikutuksilla. Jatkossa huomio pitäisi siirtää siihen, mitkä keinot todella muuttavat työuria, uravalintoja ja palkkakehitystä”, sanoo Mika Maliranta, Työn ja talouden tutkimus Laboren johtaja.

title: Hispania Nostra marks its 50th anniversary with its 45th Forum of Cultural Associations and Heritage Managers in Valencia
content:
Hispania Nostra, Europa Nostra’s country representation in Spain, held its 45th Forum, entitled “50 Years Committed to the Future of Cultural Heritage”, in Valencia  from 1 to 3 October 2026. Marking the 50th anniversary of Hispania Nostra, the Forum provided a meeting place for heritage professionals, associations and organisations to reflect on the evolution of heritage protection, the contribution of cultural associations and the future of cultural and natural heritage in Spain. Europa Nostra’s Advocacy and Partnerships Manager Vanessa Fraga Prol contributed to the Forum. 

Photo: Courtesy of Hispania Nostra

Organised annually, the Forum brings together professionals, members, associations and other individuals and organisations committed to the defence and protection of cultural and natural heritage. It offers a space to discuss a selected theme, share experiences and exchange views on current challenges and future priorities.

title: Art and anarchy in troubled times
content: In resisting authoritarianism, contemporary artists may risk more than severe backlashes – their lives may also end up on the line: in Ukraine, the anarchist transforms into a soldier; in Belarus, they are imprisoned. And when the Russian state is your homeland, avoiding conscription and attention becomes a mark of resistance.

title: In Kyrgyzstan, persons with disabilities are collecting proof of physical barriers to hold the government accountable
content:
Physical barriers are being exposed by those who are affected the most

Originally published on Global Voices

Participants of the Oasis Data Lab workshop in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Image by the public fund Oasis. Used with permission.

This interview is part of a series of spotlights on the work of some of the grantees of the Digital Spark granting scheme, as part of the Regional Support Mechanism EECA project, implemented by the Metamorphosis Foundation and TechSoup, in partnership with CIVICUS and under the Digital Democracy Initiative (DDI) that covers the Global South. It is being published on Global Voices as part of a content-sharing agreement.

Kyrgyzstan’s progress in creating an inclusive and accessible environment for people with disabilities remains limited after seven years of ratifying the United Nations (UN) Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2019.

Despite a legal responsibility to undertake measures that would remove legal and physical barriers and help people with disabilities lead independent social and economic lives, the government has not prioritized this commitment at the level requested by the country’s disabled community.

title: Kazakhstan Women Need Action on Domestic Violence
content:
During its October 6 review by the United Nations Committee on the Elimination of Discrimination against Women (CEDAW), Kazakhstan pledged new legislation to make domestic violence a standalone crime – a timely commitment. Now the government should turn words into action.

On September 23, Zhazira Adauova, a mother of two, died after her ex-husband stabbed her 16 times in Astana, Kazakhstan’s capital. Zhazira’s family told the media she had repeatedly reported threats and violence to police. Four former police officers are under investigation for alleged negligence in handling her case. 

Elvira Erkebayeva, from western Kazakhstan, endured two decades of domestic violence, including having boiling water thrown in her face. Instead of protecting her and holding her former husband accountable, authorities prosecuted Elvira in 2025 for allegedly conspiring to murder him because she wanted to “find a firearm.” 

As in manyother cases, Kazakh authorities failed to protect women who sought protection against further violence, even when they had obtained multiple protection orders. Perpetrators are often held accountable only after killing their victims.

title: Brexit Will End and Europe Will Come Together Again
content:
By Jonathan Power

LUND, Sweden | 14 October 2026 (IDN) — At last, a British prime minister who is not afraid to say Europe is good for Britain. After a slow start on the issue, Andy Burnham has now made it fairly clear that Britain will seek to rejoin the European Union. It is not going to happen tomorrow, but it will surely not take 10 years to complete the entry negotiations, as some commentators are saying. Once completed, Britain will be able to go forward once again. It will be joining a success- a continent for thousands of years riven by war, but since 1945 has had no wars among its members. (Ex-Yugoslavia and Ukraine have never been members.)

The European Union is certainly not failing. In fact, it is about to get stronger. Adding the second-largest European economy will strengthen it. The British have learnt their lesson. So have the European Union members, albeit in a different way.

title: Building the Hero Award: The Story Behind Taekyeom Lee’s 3D-Printed Model of the Internet Archive
content:
Taekyeom Lee is an educator, designer, maker, and researcher.

The associate professor of graphic design at Indiana University Bloomington is not only committed to teaching his students, Lee believes in sharing knowledge of art and design that inspires the broader community.

In 2021, Lee was an artist-in-residence at the Internet Archive in San Francisco. Fascinated by art featured in the Archive’s collection, he wanted to turn the works on the page and screen into a tactile experience.

Lee has built 3D printers based on the open-source project, RepRap. During the residency, he took a book about Korean ceramics published in 1966 from the archive’s collection, traced the shapes and turn them into 3D models, and built a DIY 3D Printer  to make physical small-scale vases out of clay. Lee documented the process and created a series of videos for others to replicate the machine to print clay with an open-source plan.

title: Suomi isännöi kouluruokakoalition huippukokouksen 2027
content:
Suomi isännöi kansainvälisen kouluruokakoalition huippukokouksen Helsingissä lokakuussa 2027.

Suomi toimii kouluruokakoalition seuraavan huippukokouksen isäntänä. Valtiosihteeri Tuomas Tapio julkisti asian kouluruokakoalition ydinryhmän kokouksessa Roomassa 14. lokakuuta 2026.

Kouluruokakoalitiossa on mukana 113 valtiota, kuusi alueellista organisaatiota ja yli 160 kumppania. Koalition tavoitteena on, että kaikilla koululaisilla on mahdollisuus kouluruokailuun vuoteen 2030 mennessä. Suomi on vuonna 2021 perustetun koalition perustajajäsen ja yksi puheenjohtajista. Kouluruokakoalitio on yksi nopeimmin viime vuosina laajentuneista monenkeskisistä aloitteista maailmassa.

Roomassa pidetyssä ydinryhmän ministeriökokouksessa julkistettiin myös kouluruokakoalition neljänneksi yhteispuheenjohtajaksi Kenia, joka tulee jatkossa toimimaan koalitiossa johtoroolissa Suomen, Ranskan ja Brasilian rinnalla.

Ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavio toimii koalition korkean tason lähettiläänä ja edustaa Suomea ministeritasolla.

title: Russia Detains Japanese Journalist on Espionage Charges
content:
Russia has arrested a Japanese journalist on suspicion of espionage, accusing him of collecting defense-related information for a Japanese intelligence agency. The reporter was detained Tuesday in the far eastern Sakhalin region, a day before he was due to leave the country, according to a Tuesday statement by the Russian Federal Security Service (FSB). The journalist was transferred to Moscow where a district court ordered his pretrial detention.

Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova identified the journalist as Yuki Imai, a correspondent for the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper. Confirming the espionage charges, she claimed Tokyo is using credentialed reporters to gather intelligence and said the incident would further damage bilateral relations, which have deteriorated over the war in Ukraine and Japan’s military policies.

title: Soviet-Era Illustrations of J. R. R. Tolkien’s The Hobbit (1976)
content: Until I read J. R. R. Tolkien’s The Lord of the Rings, my favorite book growing up was, by far, The Hobbit. Growing up in Russia, however, meant that instead of Tolkien’s English version, my parents read me a Russian translation. To me, the translation easily matched the pace and wonder of Tolkien’s original. Looking back, The Hobbit probably made such an indelible impression on me because Tolkien’s tale was altogether different than the Russian fairy tales and children’s stories that I had previously been exposed to. There were no childish hijinks, no young protagonists, no parents to rescue you when you got into trouble. I considered it an epic in the truest literary sense.

title: New Mexico and El Paso Spent Millions on Climate Plans. Three New Data Centers Could Undo Them.
content:
Last December, New Mexico officials celebrated publication of a plan to address climate change, designed to dramatically reduce the state’s greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. A few months later, just across the state line in Texas, El Paso city officials adopted their own such plan with a similar ambition. 

Each report cost millions of dollars to draft, but neither one took into account how the construction of data centers could upend climate goals in both places. 

Work is underway in Doña Ana County in southern New Mexico on one of the largest data center developments in the country: Project Jupiter, built by Austin-based Oracle. Twenty miles away in El Paso, construction is underway on another massive data center, this one built by Meta Platforms. 

A third, larger data center project is planned less than a 30-minute drive from the Meta site, on the Fort Bliss Army post in east El Paso.

The data centers are “going to undo a lot of the very expensive and very meaningful work a lot of people are doing,” New Mexico state climatologist Dave DuBois told El Paso Matters.

title: How a tiny Caribbean island shrugged off Trump’s AI rebrand
content:
LONDON — Anguilla, a Caribbean island just 16 miles long, has had to reassure its inhabitants that U.S. President Donald Trump’s attempts to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence” will not tank its economy.

Anguilla owns the .ai domain name, and since the AI boom began, a significant chunk of the island’s revenues have come from people registering for .ai websites. Trump’s attempt to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence” caused concern that the island’s income could be damaged.

But Anguillian technology minister José Vanterpool told a government press conference on Monday that the tiny island does not foresee a dent in demand for .ai domain names in the long term, and that since Trump’s recent “super intelligence” announcements sales have actually increased.

“I want to reassure the general public that at this stage, we have no reason to believe that this announcement poses an immediate threat to Anguilla’s .ai domain industry,” said Vanterpool, referring to Trump.

title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time preview – Link faces his scariest challenge yet: the 4K era
content:
The kingdom of Hyrule has been prettified, the soundtrack is newly orchestrated and our hero feels strikingly different under the thumbs … we play a hands-on demo of Nintendo’s Switch 2 remake of a 1998 game-changer

When beloved art is revisited and revised, a familiar cry is often heard: “You’re ruining my childhood!” But with Nintendo’s Switch 2 remake of Ocarina of Time, there are also livelihoods at risk: specifically, the man running the shooting gallery in Castle Town. In the original 1998 version of the game, he’d rip off players as they funnelled rupees and fudged the then still novel analogue-stick aiming. But in 2026 we have more responsive frame rates and a motion-controlled slingshot that allows precision adjustments. His targets tumble on the first go, and with them his entire business model. Even in Hyrule, the death of the high street seems inevitable.

title: How one of the world’s biggest music stars is transforming the Spanish language
content:
According to the Royal Spanish Academy (RAE, under its Spanish acronym), a “piquete” is either a sharp object, a small wound, or a group of striking workers blocking access to a workplace. It is a word, generally speaking, of conflict and harm.

But when Puerto Rican musician Benito Antonio Martínez Ocasio – more commonly known as Bad Bunny – intones on his song NUEVAYoL “Tú tiene’ piquete mami, yo también” (“You’ve got piquete mami, and so do I”), he is not talking about trade unions or pointy sticks. He is referring to something else altogether, a way of moving through the world with a certain self confidence, attitude and style.

In Puerto Rico’s boricua dialect, the meaning of piquete is totally divorced from the RAE’s official uses. But unapologetic use of his native dialect is what defines the music of the world’s biggest Spanish-language musician.

Bad Bunny has put Spanish on more global stages than any other artist in recent history, yet he is also widely criticised for his way of speaking. This is rife on social media, where users complain that he “doesn’t talk properly”, he is “deforming the language”, and “doesn’t enunciate clearly”.

title: From ‘A Little Princess’ to ‘Black Panther,’ how Hollywood films have reimagined the South Asian epic ‘Ramayana’
content:
American audiences will be able to watch an English-dubbed version of “Ramayana,” a Hindi film based on a South Asian epic tradition, in theaters in November 2026.

The Sanskrit “Ramayana,” or “Journey of Rama,” is an epic poem that was composed sometime between 400 B.C.E. and 400 C.E. The epic follows Rama, an exiled prince and an incarnation of the Hindu god Vishnu, as he journeys to rescue his wife, Sita, from the demon king Ravana.

For hundreds of years, people from different religious traditions across South Asia have retold the “Ramayana” through dramas, narrative poems, shadow puppet plays, pageants, folk songs, comics, television shows and many other mediums. Director Nitesh Tiwari’s upcoming “Ramayana” film is the latest retelling of this epic tradition.

For over a decade, I have studied how South Asian epics have been retold within and outside the Indian subcontinent. While many American moviegoers may not recognize the word “Ramayana,” they may have already encountered its characters and stories on the big screen.

Sen kirkkaat vedet, vähäinen suolaisuus ja monipuoliset merenpohjat tarjoavat elinympäristöjä lukuisille lajeille rakkohaurusta punaleviin, sinisimpukoihin ja kilkkiin. Näyttelyssä kävijä pääsee sukeltamaan pinnan alle vedenalaisten valokuvien ja videoiden johdattamana sekä tutustumaan meren eliöyhteisöihin ja niiden tutkimiseen. Näyttely tarkastelee Selkämeren vedenalaista luontoa elinympäristöjen näkökulmasta, rakkohauruniityiltä ja punaleväpohjilta syville merenpohjille ja mataliin merenlahtiin. Samalla näyttely avaa vedenalaisen luonnon monimuotoisuutta tavalla, joka jää useimmilta rannalla liikkujilta kokematta.

title: Tutkimus: Mökkeily jättää ympäristöön yhä suuremman jäljen
content:
Suomessa on noin puoli miljoonaa mökkiä, ja vuosittain noin 2,4 miljoonaa suomalaista viettää vapaa-aikaa mökkeillen. Vapaa-ajan asuminen onkin vakiintunut tärkeäksi osaksi suomalaista kulttuuria. Mökkeily mielletään usein luonnonläheiseksi ja rauhalliseksi elämäntavaksi. Siihen liittyvät ympäristövaikutukset ovat kuitenkin moninaisia, ja osa niistä on viime vuosina jopa voimistunut.

Itä-Suomen yliopiston tiedotteen mukaan Mervi Hiltusen väitöstutkimus tarkastelee suomalaista vapaa-ajan asumista ympäristökysymyksenä. Tutkimuksessa huomio kiinnittyy erityisesti mökkeilyyn liittyvään liikkumiseen, rantarakentamiseen, asumisen muutoksiin ja kulutukseen. Lisäksi tutkimus osoittaa, että mökkeilystä voi tehdä ympäristöystävällisempää, eikä mökkikulttuurin tarvitse kadota.

Hiltusen tutkimuksen mukaan mökkeilyn ympäristövaikutuksia lisäävät muun muassa yksityisautoilun kasvu, rantarakentaminen sekä hyvin varusteltujen vapaa-ajan asuntojen yhä ympärivuotisempi käyttö.

title: Burnham’s Big Test: Sparking a British Tech Revolution
content:
It’s a dispiriting and familiar pattern: Britain comes up with world-class ideas and startups, only to see them sold off, moved abroad, or left without the capital to pursue pilot production, customers, and manufacturing. 

Prime Minister Burnham wants to change this cycle. In his first speeches as UK leader, he outlined ambitious plans to reindustrialize, emphasizing artificial intelligence, chips, and drones. The targets are spot on. But the unanswered question is whether Burnham can turn good ideas into concrete outcomes.

Success will require close cooperation with European and American allies, encouraging foreign investment, and linking with Western supply chains. Scarce public funds should be invested in Cambridge and other existing successful tech clusters. Public procurement, particularly defense, should create credible lead customers. Private capital must be mobilized from pension funds and the country’s strong aviation companies.

title: French High School Student Protests Met with Excessive Force
content:
Images from ongoing student protests in France of heavily armed riot police using tear gas, stun grenades, batons, rubber bullets, and rough restraint techniques on children have sparked national and international concern.

High schoolers across France have taken to the streets since September 21 frustrated with the government’s continued under-investment in their education, which has resulted in a shortage of teachers, too large classes, and inadequate school buildings. While schools have been blockaded and some protesters have engaged in violence, the protests have been overwhelmingly peaceful.

Police use of force in response to the protests has resulted in serious injuries to children, including a 15-year-old boy who lost a hand to an explosive police stun grenade and a 14-year-old boy whose jaw shattered from a police tear-gas canister fired at close range. The government announced a temporary suspension of the use of stun grenades.

title: The world has a new answer to disinformation. But is it asking the right questions?
content:
From the UN to the EU, “information integrity” has become a guiding principle for protecting democracy and strengthening the information environment. A new NORDIS policy brief examines what the concept promises, what it overlooks – and why the same solutions may not work everywhere.

The fight against disinformation has a new vocabulary. Governments and international organisations increasingly speak of information integrity – a concept intended to address not only false and misleading information, but also the wider conditions that shape how people access, share and trust information.

In just a few years, the term has gained prominence in policy frameworks developed by the United Nations, the OECD, the European Union and the Council of Europe.

But what does information integrity actually mean? And can a concept broad enough to encompass journalism, artificial intelligence, elections, media literacy and public trust provide meaningful solutions to the challenges facing different societies?

These are among the questions explored in a new NORDIS policy brief, Interrogating Information Integrity: What the Concept Includes, What It Misses, and What Comes Next.

title: Bank of America Fined $1.21B Over AML Failures
content:
U.S. authorities imposed more than $1.21 billion in penalties on Bank of America on Tuesday over failures in its anti-money laundering controls and apparent violations of U.S. sanctions, in what the Treasury Department called the third-largest enforcement penalty in its history.

The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) assessed a $1.2 billion penalty, saying the bank failed to adequately detect and report financial activity involving priority national-security and illicit-finance risks, including Chinese money-laundering networks and activity along the U.S. southwestern border. Regulators said Bank of America failed to report more than $5 billion in suspicious transactions, including more than $1 billion linked to such priority risks.

As part of the FinCEN resolution, Bank of America admitted to willfully violating the Bank Secrecy Act, including by failing to maintain an adequate anti-money laundering program, conduct required due diligence on correspondent accounts for foreign banks, and file suspicious activity reports. The bank must also use an independent third party to identify and report suspicious activity its systems previously missed.

title: Ukrainian officers warn Starlink slowdown ‘comparable to a nuclear strike against us’
content:
Ukrainian frontline soldiers are alarmed that Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite service is reportedly being restricted on fast-moving military platforms, warning of severe operational consequences.

“This is comparable to a nuclear strike against us. All operations are on hold. This will cost many of us our lives,” an experienced Ukrainian officer told POLITICO and the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network.

The officer commands a medium-range drone strike unit in southeastern Ukraine. The unit relies heavily on Starlink for the operation and navigation of its American-made Hornet drones, used to strike targets at a range of up to 150 kilometers.

“Since last night, all Starlink and Starshield terminals used by our forces have been subject to a speed limit of 100 kilometers per hour,” the officer said.

POLITICO talked to three frontline soldiers, who all spoke on condition of being granted anonymity, as well as a Ukrainian defense ministry spokesperson and the EU’s top defense official.

The reported restrictions have revived a question Ukrainian commanders have worried about for years: how much of the country’s battlefield communications can rely on a service controlled by a U.S. company.

title: Tool and target: US law enforcement grapple with AI-enabled terrorism and anti-tech extremism
content:
From the FBI to local police departments, US authorities are increasingly warning of would-be terrorists using chatbots to plan attacks and anti-AI extremist threats

In May 2025, a 25-year-old man detonated a car bomb outside a Palm Springs fertility clinic, killing himself and injuring four others. For many, it was a wake-up call about the threats to reproductive care facilities. For the FBI, though, it was also a sign of what the agency had feared for years: bad actors were using generative AI to plan and execute terror plots.

The suspect used an unnamed generative AI tool that failed to detect his request for bomb-making instructions, law enforcement officers wrote in a previously unreported document reviewed by the Guardian. The privacy of his conversation with the AI chatbot hindered alerting police that someone was looking up how to make a bomb, according to the memo.

How extremists could use AI to devise attacks and recruit new members

How AI could be used to disseminate and produce everything from deepfakes to election misinformation and child sexual abuse material (CSAM)

How people seeking information on how to make weaponry or bombs could use AI to circumvent police detection

title: In Mali, from the Wagner Group to Africa Corps: Will Impunity Continue?
content:
When Africa Corps officially began operations in Mali in June 2025, few people held out hope that it would help alleviate the suffering of civilians in Mali, caused on the one hand by armed groups in Azawad and members from the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM), but also by the army and its auxiliaries from the Russian private military company known as Wagner.

Troops from Africa Corps, under the direct control of the Kremlin, had already begun deploying in the country as early as January 2025 and were gradually taking over Wagner’s role in support of the army’s military operations. Joint patrols by the army and Wagner between 2023 and 2025 were marred by serious violations which we recently detailed again in a report, some of which we believe amount to war crimes.

In particular, we document seven incidents in which 34 people were deliberately killed during these patrols. The victims – all civilians, according to the testimonies collected – were shot, had their throats slit, and were burned; some were even mutilated after death. Many of them were shot in cold blood while they were herding their livestock or after being apprehended.

title: Art Can Tell Ukraine’s Truth, Says Oscar Winner Chernov
content:
Speaking after receiving a Freedom Fighter Award from the Center for European Policy Analysis (CEPA), Chernov, who won an Oscar for 20 days in Mariupol, said there would be an intense battle to tell the story of the war and the truth must prevail.

“It is challenging to talk about the importance of art or cinema because we have very limited power to change the events; we cannot stop missiles, we cannot stop bullets,” he said. “What art can do, what cinema can do, is to defend the truth because when the war is over, and every war someday will be over, another battle will start, the battle for truth, the battle for justice.”

Speaking in a message recorded on the frontline in Ukraine and played to a CEPA Honors Gala in Washington, Chernov said he and other filmmakers, artists and journalists will try to ensure everyone knows the facts about the war, which started in 2014 and was stepped up by Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022.

“We will keep on going,” he said. “We will keep working, and hopefully we will all be alive.”

title: Libya: Eastern Authorities Carry Out Wave of Executions
content:
(Beirut) – The Libyan Arab Armed Forces (LAAF), which controls eastern and southern Libya, has executed at least 31 people since late August 2026 following grossly unfair military trials, Human Rights Watch said today. These are the first known executions in Libya since 2010, with at least 50 more people in Gernada military prison at imminent risk of execution.

On August 23, the LAAF military prosecutor announced that 10 people had been executed by firing squad after being convicted of murder and terrorism-related offenses. Human rights groups have documented a total of at least 31 executions as of September 10. The LAAF, led by General Khalifa Haftar, should immediately halt all executions and impose a moratorium on the death penalty, Human Rights Watch said.

title: Convicted Belgian Cocaine Boss Poured Millions Into Luxury Dubai Properties
content:
Belgian drug lord Nasserdine Tarrahi, who has been convicted of drug-related offenses in three separate cases, was extradited from Dubai to Belgium on October 14, the Antwerp prosecutor’s office confirmed to OCCRP and De Tijd. 

Tarrahi, 38, was a senior figure in the “Turtles,” a Belgian-Moroccan gang that specialized in retrieving South American cocaine from containers passing through the port of Antwerp. Later in his career he fled to Dubai, where he continued to run drug trafficking operations from the Emirati city-state, according to the most recent court verdict against him, issued in May. 

But although Belgian justice has finally caught up with him, authorities have struggled to confiscate the proceeds of his crimes, which a court in Antwerp estimated could amount to 5 million euros ($5.5 million). They only managed to find the equivalent of around $20,000 in cash, plus an assortment of exercise equipment crammed into an apartment in Antwerp he used as a base for drug trafficking.

title: EU’s cyber unit turns to AI to fend off ‘high-risk’ hacks
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission’s cybersecurity division is rolling out a plan to use artificial intelligence to respond to high-risk cyberattacks, according to a document obtained by POLITICO.

The undated document, written by the Commission’s IT department, sets out how to prepare the EU executive’s cyber defenses for “emerging AI-driven threats.” It proposes an action plan to shore up defenses in light of AI, with the most urgent move being the speed of response to attacks.

Governments have rushed to grapple with the rising threat brought by AI’s ability to expose and exploit cybersecurity vulnerabilities. Incidents like OpenAI’s accidental intrusion into Hugging Face have prompted calls, including at the highest political level, to be more wary of advanced AI models.

Being able to respond quickly to cyberattacks is most crucial in “high-risk scenarios,” the EU executive’s internal cyber defenders warned, saying that the ability to detect an attack is “not sufficient if containment measures cannot be taken quickly enough.”

title: French school protests: a rite of passage – and the result of genuine concerns
content:
Across France, school students have taken to the streets to protest about teacher shortages, dilapidated school buildings and long school days.

While the tradition of student protest has long roots in France, the country’s current fiscal crisis combined with entrenched structural problems with teacher recruitment, sickness absence and a backlog of school maintenance means this is unlikely to be something the current government can easily address.

Problems – and protests – regarding conditions in French schools go back decades.

I’ve spent 20 years conducting research in France and protest has been a recurring theme. Many research participants I’ve worked with have spoken with fondness about protesting as high school students.

One participant in Nanterre, who went on to become a community activist, repeatedly spoke about how schools in poor Paris suburbs were institutions that would “crush you”. This was due in part to French educational culture, but also because of their under-resourcing and poor state of repair. To them protest felt like an outlet for these grievances.

title: European Governments Fall Short on Reparatory Justice
content:
A United Nations Human Rights Council resolution on October 7 calling for concrete action against systemic racism should have been an opportunity for governments to demonstrate their commitment to racial justice.

Instead, the United Kingdom called for a vote, breaking from last year’s consensus on the annually tabled resolution.

Citing concerns about the applicability of international law to establish responsibility and accountability for colonial harm, the UK objected to language on reparations and then abstained from the vote; European Union members of the Council also abstained. Regardless, the resolution passed with 30 votes in favor, 17 abstentions, and none against.

The loss of last year’s consensus reveals the gap between the UK and other European governments’ stated dedication to combat racism and their actual political willingness to address its historical roots.

title: The Maldives Plans to Offer Residency to the World’s Ultra Rich – And Create Islands From Scratch to Do It
content:
Once an isolated haven for scuba divers searching for technicolor marine life, the shallow turquoise waters of the Noonu Atoll in the Maldives are in the midst of a makeover.

A fleet of dumper trucks, excavators, forklifts, and cranes has moved into the habitat for protected parrot fish and nurse sharks to sculpt 25 artificial islands and islets from over six million cubic metres of sand dredged from the seabed. 

Known as Project Ayla, the $790 million private development will host over 70 luxury dwellings and represents the vanguard of a new government strategy to lure the high-net-worth crowd to the debt-saddled nation. 

A view of the main worksite island for Project Ayla in July 2026. CREDIT: Hassan Moosa/Maldives Independent

Yet beyond the plumes of coral-smothering sediment churned up by the dredgers, opposition politicians and transparency advocates are warning of an even murkier threat: the prospect of a new international tax shelter and potential money-laundering hub carved from the ocean floor.

title: Still, We Rise: a new EU-funded programme to strengthen women’s influence in peace processes
content:
On 6 October 2026, the EU-funded programme Still, We Rise: Reclaiming and Transforming the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) Agenda was launched in Brussels. The event brought together policymakers, peacebuilding practitioners, civil society representatives and experts to discuss how women’s influence and leadership in peace processes can be strengthened at a time when the need has never been greater.

The programme is being launched against a backdrop of rising violent conflict worldwide and continuing barriers to women’s meaningful participation in efforts to build peace. Despite decades of advocacy and evidence demonstrating the value of inclusive peace processes, women remain significantly underrepresented in formal negotiations and mediation efforts. In 2024, women made up just 7 per cent of negotiators and 14 per cent of mediators in formal peace processes, and many talks included no women at all.

Discussions at the launch highlighted a key message: women are already building peace. The task now is to ensure they have the influence, resources and political support to shape peace processes and outcomes. Photo: Johanna de Tessières

title: "Musk": Alex Gibney on New Film, Legal Threats & Elon Musk Spending $366M to Help GOP in Midterms
content:
We speak with the Academy Award-winning director Alex Gibney about his new documentary Musk, an expansive, nearly four-hour examination of the world’s first trillionaire and how he has amassed unprecedented power in business, technology and politics. The film traces Elon Musk’s early ventures and the rise of SpaceX and Tesla, examining the role of government support in their growth. It also explores his acquisition of Twitter, now X; his alliance with President Donald Trump and the MAGA movement; and his role in the Department of Government Efficiency, or DOGE, whose cuts devastated federal programs, including USAID.

Gibney says Musk has carefully crafted an image of a “polymath” who can solve the world’s most pressing problems, but that he is really “kind of a ruthless businessman” willing to do whatever it takes to succeed, including “a series of elaborate cons” to win government support for his companies.

title: EU enlargement: Could new members face 15 years of oversight?
content:
The European Commission has presented MEPs with proposals to prepare the EU for a larger membership. The package sets out five areas for reform, from limiting national veto powers and expanding gradual integration to introducing safeguards designed to “hit hard” against countries that breach EU rules after joining. Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos argues that new members will not weaken the bloc but help make it fit for the future.

Presenting the Commission’s enlargement package in Strasbourg on 6 October, Kos described it as an “insurance policy” against democratic backsliding following enlargement. The package proposes a time-limited system of safeguards that would subject new member states to special oversight for up to 15 years after accession.

In cases of serious breaches of EU values, the mechanism could allow a country’s voting rights in the Council of the EU to be suspended. Kos said such protections were necessary to “protect ourselves”, pointing to “lessons from previous enlargements”.

For Kos, enlargement is not simply about bringing more countries into the EU. It is also an opportunity to make the Union stronger, more flexible and better equipped to take decisions.

title: As Federal Court Rules ALPRs are Mass Surveillance, EFF Gets Disappointing Ruling
content:
In an extremely disappointing ruling, a California trial court dismissed SIREN v. San Jose, our case challenging the city of San Jose’s warrantless searches of its vast stores of automated license plate reader (ALPR) data. EFF and the ACLU of Northern California represent SIREN and CAIR California, two non-profits that serve San Jose residents, in this case.

Make no mistake: We believe this ruling is wrong on the law, and we will appeal. The ruling ignores the importance of landmark rulings from the U.S. Supreme Court regarding the invasiveness of aggregating collected data on an individual over time, including one issued just months ago. It also severely underestimates the harm that ALPRs cause, in San Jose and around the country.

Donald Insall was a pioneering conservationist, architect, planning consultant, author and teacher; he founded Donald Insall Associates in 1958, one of Britain’s leading conservation practices.

title: After flood disasters, Nepal needs clear numbers on aid and a reconstruction plan
content:
Nepali communities live in the shadow of natural hazards, where uncertainty and fear are daily realities

Originally published on Global Voices

Settlements across the Tadi River, Devighat in Nuwakot District. Image via Susmita Aryal on October 7, 2026. Used with permission.

Forty-six days later, just when Nepal was trying to recover from the Bhotekoshi flash flood, which struck the Nepal–Tibet border regions, affecting Rasuwa and Nuwakot, another landslide-induced flood hit Chumnubri, Gorkha, on October 11, 2026. This latest disaster has added to the wounds of communities who live in the shadow of natural hazards, where uncertainty and fear are daily realities.

The climate-related disaster in Nuwakot has devastated a once-popular tourist landscape, destroying its natural beauty and economic opportunities, with settlements heartbreakingly reduced to rubble and vital infrastructure, including roads, bridges and hydro-power facilities, washed away. The full death toll remains officially unconfirmed.

Survivors still come to search for their belongings in Devighatm, Nuwakot District. Image via Susmita Aryal on October 7, 2026. Used with permission.

title: Saudi Arabia: Death Penalty for Facebook Comment
content:
(Beirut) – A Saudi court has sentenced a Sri Lankan migrant worker to death over a Facebook comment that was deemed blasphemous, Human Rights Watch said today. Saudi authorities should reverse the judgment and release him immediately.

The Saudi Court of Appeal in the Eastern Region handed down the death sentence to Anojan Sivarasa, 24, on September 17, 2026, after two court sessions. An initial ruling had sentenced him to five years in prison.

“Sentencing a migrant worker to death over a Facebook comment that he has publicly apologized for is an outrageous overreaction from Saudi authorities amid a surge in executions,” said Joey Shea, senior Saudi Arabia researcher at Human Rights Watch. “No one should face execution for a comment on religion.”

title: Afgaaninaisen katse: Gulsuum osallistuu naisten Facebook-kapinointiin salaa veljiltään – ”Pienikin virhe voisi vaarantaa sekä oman että perheeni hengen”
content:
On varhainen aamu Afganistanin koillisosassa sijaitsevassa Parwanin maakunnassa. Ilmassa tuntuu aamun tuntien tyyneys, ja vain harvojen ohikulkijoiden askeleet rikkovat hiljaisuuden.

Erään kaupungin vaatimattomimpiin kuuluvissa kodeissa asuu 28-vuotias Gulsuum (nimi muutettu), joka elää oikeastaan kahta elämää.

Naapureidensa silmissä hän on hiljainen nuori nainen, joka käy ostamassa ruokaa, asuu perheensä luona ja yrittää elää tavallista arkea. Tämän julkisivun takana on kuitenkin ihminen, joka taistelee salanimen suojissa afganistanilaisnaisten koulutuksen, vapauden ja ihmisarvon puolesta.

Hän esiintyy nimellä Gulsuum suojatakseen henkilöllisyyttään. Hänen pelkonsa, toiveensa ja elämäntarinansa ovat kuitenkin täyttä totta.

Gulsuum asuu isänsä, äitinsä, tätinsä ja kahden veljensä kanssa yhdellä Parwanin maakunnan asuinalueista. Hänen naimaton tätinsä on pitkään ollut erottamaton osa perhettä.

Vain täti tietää Gulsuumin salaisuuden.

Uskoin, että Afganistanin tulevaisuuden rakentaisivat tytöt.

title: Tekoälyavustaja UMAI näyttää suuntaa koko valtionhallintoon
content:
Ulkoministeriössä on kehitetty uusi, turvaluokitellun tai salassa pidettävän tiedon käsittelemisen mahdollistava tekoälyavustaja, UMAI. Sen pilotti on käynnistynyt ensimmäisillä käyttäjäryhmillä. Samalla ulkoministeriö toimii pilottiorganisaationa valtionhallinnon yhteisen tekoälyalustan kehittämisessä.

Ulkoasianhallinnossa tekoälyä hyödynnetään jo esimerkiksi tiedonhaussa, tekstien valmistelussa ja analysoinnissa. Käyttöä rajoittaa usein kuitenkin se, ettei sillä voida käsitellä kaikkea työssä tarvittavaa tietoa. UMAI:n avulla tekoälyä voidaan hyödyntää myös työtehtävissä, joissa käsitellään turvaluokiteltua TL IV -tason aineistoa tai salassa pidettäviä henkilötietoja.

Tämä laajentaa tekoälyn käyttömahdollisuuksia merkittävästi. Tekoälyn avulla voidaan tulevaisuudessa tukea esimerkiksi edustustoraportointia, tilanneanalyysien valmistelua sekä poliittisiin ja taloudellisiin kansainvälisiin suhteisiin liittyvän tiedon käsittelyä.

title: FOI reform in Germany and Mexico
content:
Dear friend,

We can’t take our Freedom of Information laws for granted — as we’ve seen through the years with governmental pushback both in the UK, and in countless countries around the world.

In this free webinar, we’ll hear from those at the frontline of defending the right to know in Germany and Mexico, two countries where recent changes have raised important questions about the future of Access to Information.

In Germany, FragDenStaat say that they are facing "the most serious attack on transparency in the history of the Federal Republic and a threat to our democracy", with a proposed scrapping of ATI. In Mexico, a change in the agency responsible for FOI has undermined public access to information, ruling against most requests.

We hope you’ll join us on Oct 26 to hear these fascinating stories, and what civil society is doing to kick back against such challenges: find out more and book here.

Veza is Strategic Campaigner at FragDenStaat (Ask the State) in Germany.

Like mySociety's WhatDoTheyKnow, FragDenStaat provides a simple way for citizens to submit FOI requests online; and they also campaign very actively around information rights.

title: An Inside Look At How To Tame Unstoppable AI
content:
Earlier this year, a university decided to audit the effectiveness of its new AI system designed to help answer student questions. So, university officials hired me, an AI auditor, to come take a look. During my review, I discovered that the AI agent, which was supposed to handle only general questions about the academic calendar and organizational matters, had started opening students’ personal records — accessing data that wasn’t needed to answer their questions. The chatbot, however, did nothing further with that information.

When the university’s engineers, at the time, learned what happened from the access logs, they fixed it, and that was that. There was no official record. No internal rule required them to record such incidents, and nobody was assigned to track events like this. It was simply part of the engineering team’s bug-fixing process. The incident was what I call a near miss, and near misses are what a reporting system exists to catch. The same behavior could lead to something more serious next time, and we only know about this case because the university voluntarily brought me in to examine the system.

title: Hackers Turn French Supermarket Refrigerators Into Furnaces
content:
A massive cyberattack targeted hundreds of French supermarkets overnight on October 11 to 12, remotely hijacking refrigeration systems to trigger intense defrost cycles, spoiling vast quantities of food and sparking fires.

The unprecedented incident has triggered a national criminal investigation. The Paris Prosecutor's Office confirmed to OCCRP Tuesday that its cybercrime section has initiated an investigation, entrusted to the Anti-Cybercrime Office (OFAC). The probe aims to "identify the victims and establish a link between the incident and the damage reported by them, specifically regarding food spoilage and the outbreak of fires."

Hackers gained remote control of the store refrigeration systems by exploiting internet-connected controllers. The attack methodology mirrors vulnerabilities the operational technology security firm Claroty warned the industry about two months prior. In a prescient August report titled "Freeze the Controller, Defrost the Food," the firm's Team82 research division warned about the possibility that hackers could access Danfoss refrigeration systems to bypass security and manipulate temperatures.

title: The Names of Nearly 4 Million Enslaved People in Former British Colonies Are Now Searchable Online, Helping Descendants Find Lost Ancestors
content:
A few years ago, we featured here on Open Culture the Freedmen’s Bureau Project database, which contains searchable information on formerly enslaved people in the United States after its Civil War. With nearly 1.8 million men, women, and children registered there when it first opened to the public, it has remained a valuable resource for many Americans researching their own heritage, not just descendants of former slaves but of other Civil War refugees as well. But of course, the U.S. was hardly the only country where slavery existed. Countless people here in the twenty-first century have ancestors who were enslaved in other former British colonies, and now they’ve got a portal through which to do genealogical searches of their own.

Launched by a partnership between the genealogy company Ancestry and the Centre for the Study of the Legacies of British Slavery at University College London, the online Former British Colonies Enslavement Registers makes available records on nearly four million individuals enslaved between 1813 and 1840 in a host of countries from the Bahamas to Mauritius to South Africa.

title: Vieraskynä: Kun piiloon jäävä todellisuus tuodaan museoon
content:
Kulttuuripalvelujen käyttäminen ei useinkaan ole ensimmäisenä mielessä ihmisellä, joka elää asunnottomana tai muussa vakavassa asumisen kriisissä. Huomio suuntautuu siihen, miten arjen välttämättömät tarpeet järjestyvät ja mistä saa apua.

Museoon menemistä voivat rajoittaa pääsymaksujen lisäksi monet näkymättömämmät kynnykset. Museo saattaa tuntua vieraalta paikalta, ja osallistumista voivat vaikeuttaa asunnottomuuteen liittyvä stigma, häpeän kokemukset, kuormittava elämäntilanne sekä tunne siitä, ettei museo ole tarkoitettu “minunlaisilleni” ihmisille.

Siksi kulttuuripalvelujen saavutettavuus ei ole asunnottomuutta kokevien ihmisten näkökulmasta toissijainen kysymys. Se kertoo siitä, ketkä tunnistetaan yhteiskunnan täysivaltaisiksi jäseniksi ja keiden kokemusten katsotaan kuuluvan yhteiseen kulttuuriin ja historiaan.

Yhteistyömme esimerkiksi Arkkitehtuuri- ja designmuseon kanssa on ollut merkityksellistä. Siihen on kuulunut asiantuntijuuden vaihtoa, Arkkitehtuuri kuuluu kaikille -podcastin sisällöntuotantoa ja 2 139 -installaation eli origamitaloista koostuvan yhteisötaideteoksen rakentamista museon aulaan.

title: Kaipuu energiaomavaraisuuteen voi lisätä ilmastotoimien kannatusta
content:
Geopoliittiset jännitteet vaikuttavat myös Suomessa julkiseen keskusteluun energia- ja ilmastopolitiikasta. Ilmastotoimien kannalta on tärkeää edistää eri ryhmien yhteistä ymmärrystä niiden hyödyistä.

Vaikka enemmistö maailman ihmisistä kannattaa ilmastotoimia, niiden säätäminen ja käyttöönotto on usein poliittisesti vaikeaa. Samalla kun ilmastonmuutoksen monet negatiiviset vaikutukset jakautuvat maapallolla epätasaisesti, myöskään ilmastotoimien vaikutukset eivät ole yhtäläiset.

Kaikki toki hyötyvät pitkällä tähtäimellä elinvoimaisesta ja -kelpoisesta planeetasta. Kuitenkin lyhyellä aikavälillä toimet saattavat luoda häviäjiä – niitä, joille politiikkatoimista koituu maksuja, ansionmenetyksiä tai muuta haitallista. Samalla toinen osa saattaa taloudellisesti suuresti hyötyä ilmastotoimista. Monet poliitikot ja puolueet ovat käyttäneet hyödykseen ilmastotoimien häviäjien epävarmuutta ja tyytymättömyyttä.

title: Scammers Are Stealing Millions From Food Stamp Recipients. Congress Could Fix It — but Won’t.
content:
It wasn’t the kind of call a grocery store gets every day. A customer with a thick Eastern European accent was on the phone saying he wanted to buy several thousand cans of Red Bull. Could the store have them in stock in a few days? Also, did they have equipment to move all those stacks of energy drinks into the parking lot, where two minivans would be waiting?

When the day came, Oct. 19, 2022, employees at the Smart & Final store in San Diego sold 3,960 cans of Red Bull and 720 of Monster Energy to two men and two women, all with the same accent, and helped them wheel the pallets out back. To pay for it all — the bill came to $10,747.05 — the group pulled out piles of plastic. These weren’t credit or debit cards; they looked more like hotel-room keys. There were 25 cards in all, each with a different amount loaded onto it, and the four people took turns swiping one after another. Then, the payment complete, they drove off.

title: Celebrating five years of strengthening open digital infrastructure
content:
Five years after the feasibility study for investing in the infrastructure of the 21st century, we look back and ahead: how do we strengthen the open source foundation of the future?

Five years ago, the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWi) commissioned a small team to work out, in a feasibility study, how public investment in open digital infrastructure could be designed. In late 2021, the Log4Shell vulnerability in Apache Log4j, a widely used open source software library, caused far-reaching damage. Log4j was running in millions of systems at the time, and the vulnerability spread along software dependencies into public administration systems and critical infrastructure worldwide. The incident exposed a dire situation hiding in plain sight. Open source technologies, from programming libraries and protocols to developer tools and software components, form the technical foundation of all modern digital systems. Yet they suffer from chronic underinvestment, and they are developed and maintained mostly by volunteers. Countless people, companies, and institutions depend on them, but few invest in maintaining them.

title: Två nya böcker i serien Värt att veta: Sport och Feminism
content:
I höst utforskar vi brännande frågor om kamp, motstånd och rörelse genom sport och feminism. Heidi Kurvinen samt Antti Kuusela och Riitta-Ilona Pummi-Kuusela förmedlar stora insikter i kompakt format på 60 sidor.

I Sport tar Antti Kuusela och Riitta-Ilona Pummi-Kuusela pulsen på idrottens motsägelsefulla värld och väsen. Den är på många sätt primitiv – ett område för tävlan och kamp – men också en arena för ideal och drömmar där människor möts. Boken utforskar idrottens historia och myter, och ställer frågor om varför människor idrottar och vilken roll sporten spelar i våra liv.

– Alla kulturer har haft någon typ av sport och det finns inte ett enda område på jorden bebott av människor där man inte skulle känna till sport, säger författarna.

I Feminism visar Heidi Kurvinen på feminismens utveckling från historisk folkrörelse till dagens globala debatt. Under mer än hundra år har rörelsen varit en drivkraft för samhällsförändring, samtidigt som den mött motstånd. Boken belyser hur synen på kön, makt och ojämlikhet har förändrats över tid och hur dagens feminism både vinner ny mark och väcker starka reaktioner.

title: OpenAI employee arrested and charged over hidden recording
content:
Federal authorities arrested a Saudi national employed at OpenAI and charged him with planting a recording device in a company’s executive conference room, the Department of Justice announced Tuesday.

On or around Sept. 30, OpenAI discovered a sophisticated recording device inserted into the back of a television in an executive conference room located in one of its San Francisco offices. The company determined that the device was installed approximately a couple days prior, concealed in toilet paper. The contents of the device were encrypted, according to the DOJ.

The Department of Justice said in a news release that the employee, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, was arrested Friday and appeared in federal court Tuesday. OpenAI confirmed the incident on social media and said that it was supporting the FBI’s investigation.

“We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier,” OpenAI said in its statement. “At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data.”
