title: Companies rushed in on AI. Now some are pulling back
content:
Rapid AI adoption left workers cleaning up a flood of errors and low-quality work

Employers around the globe are grappling with the fallout from rushing to adopt fast-changing artificial intelligence tools.

Meta has scaled back plans to axe staff and use more AI agents after the company found employees were spending more and more time cleaning up technical and security errors, Reuters reported. And after thinning its workforce, especially middle managers, in a 2023 efficiency push, the company is expanding its managerial ranks again, LinkedIn posts from workers show.

title: Trainees explore Community Engagement
content:
How can heritage practitioners create meaningful opportunities for communities to shape the ways their heritage is understood, cared for and shared? This question guided HERITΛGE’s recent four-day online workshop, Engaging Communities in Cultural Heritage, which brought together 23 participants from 18 countries.

Participants joined from Poland, Lebanon, Italy, Iraq, Albania, Greece, Armenia, Rwanda, Serbia, Latvia, Mauritius, India, Egypt, Iran, South Africa, Kenya, Palestine and Nepal to explore 

The programme examined different understandings of community, identity, belonging and relationships with heritage, while emphasising the importance of positionality, research, inclusion, accessibility and meaningful participation. 

Participants were introduced to approaches including Asset-Based Community Development, asset mapping and ethnographic research, exploring how community assets, knowledge, relationships and networks can inform the design and implementation of engagement activities.

title: The Zine Atlas
content:
The following is a guest post by the 2025-2026 Innovator in Residence, Vivian Li. As part of her work with the Library, Vivian hosted a series of community outreach events, including zine-making workshops in partnership with the Chicago Public Library. Read on to learn how you can also make a zine and check out the end of the post to print your own copy of research zines created by Vivan about various LOC collections.

In Chicago, the Anywhere Adventures team ran a series of workshops inviting people to make zines about their neighborhood. These zines could describe a piece of history that happened on your block, a memory you have, some kind of guide, or anything you want to share and preserve about your piece of the world.

I’ve been copying and gathering these zines into a community artbook called the Zine Atlas. If you would like to make a zine and contribute it to the Atlas, or if you just want to participate in the writing prompts we used in Chicago, you can do it yourself at home!

Materials needed:
– Paper (2 sheets)
– Scissors
– Drawing supplies (just a pencil/pen is fine, but feel free to use anything!)

title: Kokeilussa uusi työkalu, joka pureutuu pikseleihin ja paljastaa peukaloinnin
content:
Maallikon silmään kuva on kuva. Konepellin alla se on kuitenkin bittejä, joiden avulla kuvatiedosto voidaan yksilöidä ja tarkistaa. Kansallisarkiston kehittämä Tarkista kuva -työkalu perustuu kahteen tekniseen ominaisuuteen: tiivisteeseen ja digitaaliseen vesileimaan.

Tarkista kuva on selainpohjainen työkalu, joka koostuu kahdesta osasta: taustalla olevasta tarkistusrekisteristä ja käyttäjälle näkyvästä tarkistustoiminnosta. Tarkistusrekisteriin arkisto tallentaa tietoa kuvista: tiivisteet ja vesileimojen tunnisteita aikaleimattuina. Aikaleima osoittaa, että nämä tiedot ovat olleet olemassa tietyllä hetkellä.

Tiiviste on tavallaan tiedoston sormenjälki. Se on algoritmilla tiedoston bittien perusteella laskettu, käytännössä yksilöllinen merkkijono. Jos tiedostosta muuttuu yksikin bitti, esimerkiksi yksi pikseli, tiivistekin muuttuu.

Digitaalinen vesileima taas on kuvan pikselidataan upotettu näkymätön tunniste. Vesileiman avulla kuva voidaan tunnistaa arkiston aineistoksi myös silloin, kun sitä on kevyesti muokattu.

title: IPCC is under pressure to delay publication of key global climate report
content:
AR7 report was scheduled for 2028 in time for Cop33 summit but some petro-states and major developing countries want to postpone it

Scientists are coming under pressure from some petro-states and major developing countries to delay publication of a key global report on the climate, despite pleas from vulnerable countries worried that postponement could spell disaster for them.

The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, the UN-convened body of the world’s leading climate scientists, is meeting this week in Addis Ababa to discuss its seventh assessment report, a comprehensive survey of all that is known about the climate crisis.

title: Englannin vihreä vallankumous lässähti
content:
Kalle Pusa

Verde pohti keväällä, kuinka korkealle Englannin, ja Walesin, vihreiden liito saattaisi yltää. Vastaus on nyt saatu. 

Ei kovin korkealle. Kevään orastava vihreä vallankumous näyttää kellastuneen syksyn sateisiin. 

Torstaina 8. lokakuuta käytiin Holborn and St. Pancrasin vaalipiirin täytevaalit, joissa Englannin vihreiden puheenjohtaja Zack Polanski hävisi Britannian työväenpuolueen eli labourin Sagal Abdi-Walille selvin lukemin. Abdi-Wali sai 12 292 ääntä, kun taas Polanski keräsi 8 928 ääntä. 

Holbornin ja St. Pancrasin vaalipiiri on ollut vuosikymmeniä labour-puolueen ydinalueita Lontoossa. Polanskin mahdollisuuksia pidettiin matalina, kun hän asettui ehdolle, mutta syksyn tapahtumat romahduttivat pienenkin toivon voitosta. 

Pääministeri Andy Burnhamin työväenpuolue voi nyt huokaista helpotuksesta. Vaaleja pidettiin testinä siitä, kuinka suosittu Burnhamin valtakausi on ollut ja kuinka paljon keväällä nousussa ollut vihreät voisi labouria haastaa.

title: Yemen Plunges Back into "Full-Scale Civil War," Houthis Trade Strikes with Saudi Arabia
content:
Yemen’s Ansar Allah, also known as the Houthis, have repeatedly attacked the Saudi capital of Riyadh in recent days. On Saturday, a missile strike on the airport in Riyadh killed at least 12 and injured over 300 in the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in over a decade. President Trump is now weighing whether to join the Saudi fight against the Houthis in Yemen.

This latest escalation comes after Ansar Allah captured key areas along Yemen’s Red Sea coastline in recent weeks, driving back the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized government and taking control of the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait.

“Yes, the Houthis are attacking Saudi Arabia with airstrikes, but there is now, actively, a real ground war going on within Yemen, and that is a far more relevant and important issue for the Yemenis on a day-to-day basis because they are now back into a full-scale civil war,” says Middle East scholar Helen Lackner.

title: Will the UK rejoin the EU? Andy Burnham’s plan has two goals, expert says
content:
Until recently, the British government was reluctant to entertain the possibility of rejoining the European Union. Now, London’s position appears to be shifting. At the Labour Party’s annual conference, Prime Minister Andy Burnham called for a debate on the future of Britain’s relationship with the EU.

“Brexit has done more harm than good,” Burnham said. He outlined several possible paths forward: maintaining the current relationship, joining the EU customs union, returning to the single market or even becoming a full member of the bloc again. On the last option, he suggested Britain could go “all the way”.

Burnham has stressed, however, that rejoining the EU remains a distant prospect. He has also suggested that another referendum might not necessarily be required.

According to Krzysztof Winkler, an analyst at the Warsaw Enterprise Institute, a Polish economic policy think tank, the prime minister’s position reflects both economic and political considerations.

“Western societies are now deeply divided between liberal-left and conservative camps. Essentially, we’re dealing with two very different ways of looking at the world,” Winkler explains.

title: Privacy's Defenders Podcast: No Privacy Without Encryption
content:
When we communicate online today – from your personal emails and DMs to secure international commerce – we usually do so with encryption. Encryption converts readable data into unreadable gibberish to protect our privacy and security. This didn’t just happen organically. Three decades ago, the U.S government treated encryption like a weapon, and it took some unlikely heroes to set it free: a grad student, a junior lawyer, and a fledgling digital rights group who sued the federal government. 

The ruling in Bernstein v. Department of Justice held that code is speech and so is protected by the First Amendment – a precedent that underpins the internet as we know it today. This landmark case was led by Cindy Cohn, then a young pro bono lawyer working on behalf of EFF, who went on to become EFF’s legal director and then executive director. 

Welcome to the second episode of “Privacy’s Defenders,” a podcast about the people – lawyers, journalists, hackers, and others – who’ve fought to secure your digital liberties since before most people even knew what the internet was. 

(You can also find this episode on the Internet Archive and on YouTube.)

title: Poetry book promotes Chabacano, Asia’s only Spanish-based creole language
content:
Ten authors and 23 poems are featured in the anthology

Originally published on Global Voices

Photo from the Facebook page of Voces del Alma. Used with permission

A new poetry anthology features writers of Chabacano, one of the Philippines’ 170 languages, which is widely spoken in the southernmost city of Zamboanga, and stands out as Asia’s only Spanish-based creole language.

The Philippines was a colony of Spain for more than three centuries, but the Spanish language was only used by the elite, friars, and colonial rulers. Only in Zamboanga did a Spanish-based creole language develop.

In 2018, Global Voices featured Bien Chabacano, a blog dedicated to promoting and documenting Chavacano de Zamboanga. Its creator, Jerome Herrera, launched a book project this year by inviting writers to submit poems to be compiled in an anthology. This led to the launch of the “Sombra y Luz” book in July, featuring 23 poems by 10 authors. The poems are mainly about love, family, and Zamboangueño identity.

title: France Shouldn’t Return Afghans to Taliban Rule
content:
France has confirmed that it has opened a “technical dialogue” with the Taliban authorities regarding forced returns to Afghanistan. The announcement marks a dangerous shift in policy that places Afghans in France at risk of persecution, torture and other grave abuses in contravention of France’s international human rights obligations.

The “technical dialogue” follows in the wake of a Taliban delegation to Brussels in June in which migration and return policies were discussed with European Union officials. Germany has already deported 263 Afghans since last year.

The French Ministry of Foreign Affairs stated that the talks aim “to facilitate the removal of Afghan nationals who are illegally on the national territory and who represent a national security risk.” French officials say the dialogue is narrowly focused but have not set out any guarantees that those at particular risk, including women, would be protected.

title: UK Sanctions Dutch Businessman Allegedly Linked to Russian Arms Firms
content:
The United Kingdom has imposed sanctions⁠ on Dutch businessman Alexander Tattersall and his Turkish company, Redwing Metal, following a joint investigation by The Kyiv Independent, OCCRP and IrpiMedia that exposed shipments of European industrial equipment to Russian factories supplying missile and fighter jet manufacturers.

Tattersall and Redwing Metal were among 38 individuals, companies and vessels targeted⁠ by the British government on October 8 as part of a broader effort to disrupt Russia’s military supply chains, oil revenues and financial networks.

The measures freeze assets under British jurisdiction and prohibit British individuals and businesses from conducting transactions with the designated parties.

The sanctions follow a June investigation⁠ by OCCRP, The Kyiv Independent and Italy’s IrpiMedia, which revealed that Redwing Metal had shipped more than $5 million worth of European-made industrial machinery to two Russian metallurgical plants in 2023 and 2024, despite EU export restrictions.

The equipment included computer-controlled lathes, metal heat-treatment furnaces, hydraulic presses and other machinery manufactured in Italy, Germany, Spain and the Czech Republic.

title: The Bialetti Moka Express: The History of Italy’s Iconic Coffee Maker, and How to Use It the Right Way
content:
I am sure that many an Open Culture reader has a Bialetti Moka Express in their kitchen. I know I do, but I must add that I knew little about its history and apparently even less about how to properly use one. Coffee expert and author of The World Atlas of Coffee James Hoffmann introduces us to the appliance we think we know in the above video.

Alfonso Bialetti didn’t originally get into the coffee business. In 1919, the Bialetti company was an aluminum manufacturer, with the Moka Express invented somewhere around 1933 by Luigi de Ponti, who worked for the company. According to Deconstructing Product Design by William Lidwell and Gerry Manacsa, the inspiration came from Bialetti’s wife’s old-fashioned washing machine: “a fire, a bucket, and a lid with a tube coming out of it. The bucket was filled with soapy water, sealed with the lid, and then brought to a boil over the fire, at which point the vaporized soapy water was pushed up through the tube and expelled on to the laundry.”

title: He Waited Nine Years in Prison for His Lawyer to File a Single Brief. In This State, There’s No Rule Against It.
content:
In 2020, seven years after he was appointed to represent a client who claimed he was wrongly convicted, attorney Scott Galloway told the judge that he was still looking into the case and needed more time.  

“I am still in the process of interviewing individuals,” the lawyer wrote to the judge in Delaware County, outside Philadelphia, who had already granted him 32 extensions. 

His client, Nolan O’Neal, had been a 20-year-old high school student when he was arrested for murder by Chester police, who had four eyewitnesses identifying him. At his 2005 trial, those witnesses all recanted, saying police had pressured them to accuse O’Neal. 

By the time Galloway joined the case, in 2013, O’Neal had already spent eight years in prison insisting he was innocent. The lawyer’s job was to help him file a petition under Pennsylvania’s Post Conviction Relief Act. That law provided a narrow path to freedom if Galloway could find crucial new evidence or prove that previous lawyers had mishandled the case.

But court records do not show that the attorney did much other than ask for more time.

title: Europe’s leaders abandon the race for frontier AI
content:
BRUSSELS — As the U.S. and China compete to train the world’s most advanced artificial intelligence models, Europe is stepping back.

European politicians and tech executives have in recent weeks shifted their focus away from frontier AI as it becomes clear the bloc has no artificial intelligence models that can compete with top American or Chinese models, and Europe’s leading contender Mistral faces questions over its performance.

Instead, a new mantra has emerged: Europe doesn’t need to own the models as long as it can put them to work.

“Striving to build a competitive frontier lab right now feels like very wishful thinking,” said Max Junestrand, CEO of Swedish AI company Legora, a €6 billion company that provides an AI tool for law firms. “I would rather see us put more thinking cycles into how do we capitalize on the technology rather than how do we try to catch up.”

The suggestion that frontier AI models are now out of reach for European AI labs comes as the most advanced models become a major global security issue.

title: The biggest threat from AI is the sense that we have no say in it. To that I say game on | Peter Lewis
content:
The tech bros and their highly paid sock puppets are banking on us giving in to their ‘inevitability doctrine’. But in Australia, and around the world, resistance is rising

Of all the drivers of the populist wave, one of the most powerful is the sense of inevitability that surrounds what we are told is the march of progress. In presenting the future as a fait accompli, it poisons the civic well by dealing us out of the game.

While the US clings on to its status as the oldest constitutional democracy, the unholy alliance between the tech overlords and the White House is creating its own AI reality untethered to the will of the people.

title: How the ‘geopolitical stigma’ associated with Putin’s Russia is affecting ordinary Russians
content:
Russia’s international standing collapsed within weeks of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Sanctions swept across Russian banks, businesses and political elites, while western companies exited the country en masse. For those living inside Russia, it was the everyday, tangible shifts that made this feel real.

Western goods disappeared from supermarket shelves, direct flights to Europe stopped and getting visas to travel abroad became more difficult. Russian athletes, artists and scholars, meanwhile, were excluded from international competitions, cultural platforms and academic events.

For Russians living elsewhere in Europe, the change was often more subtle. Questions about their nationality in job applications, negative media coverage and offhand comments about Russia all contributed to a growing sense that being Russian now meant carrying a stigma. Russia’s changing international reputation had suddenly become personal.

title: Försök med ett nytt verktyg som granskar pixlar och avslöjar manipulationer
content:
För en lekman är en bild en bild. Under ytan handlar det ändå om bitar som gör det möjligt att identifiera och kontrollera en bildfil. Verktyget Kontrollera bild som har tagits fram av Riksarkivet bygger på två tekniska funktioner: hashvärde och digital vattenstämpel.

Kontrollera bild är ett webbläsarbaserat verktyg som består av två delar: ett kontrollregister i bakgrunden och en kontrollfunktion som visas för användaren. Kontrollregistret arkiverar information om bilder: tidsstämplade identifierare för hashvärden och vattenstämplar. Tidsstämpeln visar att dessa uppgifter har funnits vid en viss tidpunkt.

Hashvärdet är på sätt och vis filens fingeravtryck. Det är en i praktiken unik sträng som har beräknats utifrån filens bitar med en algoritm. Om bara en enda bit i filen ändras, till exempel en pixel, förändras också hashvärdet.

En digital vattenstämpel är däremot en osynlig identifierare som bäddats in i bildens pixeldata. Med hjälp av vattenstämpeln kan en bild identifieras som arkivmaterial även när den har redigerats lätt.

content:

Den kompletta lösningen omfattar drönaren, RTK-basstation för noggrann positionering, fjärrkontroll och Android-enhet samt systemen RevoSpray 3 och RevoCast 3. Patrik Nordgren, Sverigechef, Mtech Digital Solutions Ab

title: Mepit vaativat EU:lta arvopohjaista Kiina-politiikkaa
content:
Euroopan parlamentti haluaa, että EU pitää Kiina-politiikassa kiinni arvoistaan, jotka liittyvät muun muassa ihmisoikeuksiin, ilmastoon, kauppaan ja turvallisuuteen. Viime viikolla hyväksytyssä suosituksessa mepit toteavat, että monikeskeisen maailmanjärjestyksen edistäminen on EU:n edun mukaista. Kiinan kanssa olisi tärkeää käydä vuoropuhelua globaaleista haasteista.

Euroopan parlamentin ja Kiinan hallituksen kontaktit olivat jäissä neljä vuotta, aina kevääseen 2025 saakka, jolloin osapuolet alkoivat purkaa rajoituksia. Syynä olivat EU:n ihmisoikeussyistä asettamat Kiina-pakotteet, minkä seurauksena Kiina asetti useita europarlaamentikkoja perheineen maahantulokieltoon.

Tänä vuonna välit ovat lämmenneet, ja jo useita Euroopan parlamentin valtuuskuntia on vieraillut Kiinassa.

Uudessa suosituksessa kuitenkin todetaan, että EU:n suhteet Kiinaan ovat kriittisessä tilassa johtuen Kiinan epäreilusta talouspolitiikasta ja kannasta Venäjän Ukrainassa käymään sotaan.

title: Planetary diet in Polish schools sparks controversy: “The biggest problem is parents”
content:
It all started with a single dish made from beans or lentils. Before long, Poland was embroiled in a heated debate over hungry schoolchildren, digestive problems and claims of forced veganism. The trigger? A new government regulation changing what can be served in school canteens.

But first, what exactly is the planetary diet? Despite claims circulating online, it is not a Polish government initiative designed to take meat off children’s menus.

The term planetary health diet gained international attention in 2019, when the EAT-Lancet Commission, an international group of scientists, proposed a way of eating that would be healthier for people and less damaging to the environment.

It is not a vegan diet. Although largely plant-based, it allows for animal products, including dairy, poultry and fish. The emphasis is on eating more vegetables, fruit, whole grains, nuts and legumes, while consuming less red meat and sugar.

Which brings us to Polish schools — and the legumes that have become an unlikely source of national controversy.

title: Japan’s Commitment to Sport Needs to Include Athlete Protection
content:
Every October, Japan celebrates Sports Day, a public holiday established to commemorate the 1964 Tokyo Olympic Games and Japan's longstanding commitment to sport as a national priority.

There has been much to celebrate in recent years. For more than six decades, Japan has had dedicated legislation – now known as the Basic Act on Sports – to advance sports on a national level. By investing in facilities, athletes’ development, and public participation—and hosting mega-events like the 2020 Olympics—Japan has become a leading sports nation.

Yet, one critical issue has received too little attention: protecting athletes and children from sports-related abuse. Human Rights Watch has documented the widespread physical, sexual, and verbal abuse many Japanese children and athletes experience when they participate in sports. A professional athlete described suffering abuses from his coach: “I was hit so many times, I can’t count ... the coach … hit [me] in the face in front of everyone. I was bleeding, but he did not stop.”

title: How Maroš Šefčovič talked his way to a China trade breakthrough
content:
Europe’s trade chief has won a first concession from Beijing. Now he must convince EU leaders that dialogue can deliver more.

By Camille Gijs and Carlo Martuscelli
in Brussels

Illustration by Natália Delgado/POLITICO

When Maroš Šefčovič set out his strategy for engaging with China to European Union ambassadors in July, he had a warning for governments urging tougher action on trade against Beijing.

“Sometimes, it’s even popular to start a trade war, but it’s very difficult to finish it,” the EU trade chief recalled later in an interview with POLITICO.

Three months on, Šefčovič has secured a first breakthrough, reaching a deal in Beijing last week to sharply reduce imports of Chinese hybrid cars. The symbolic win marks a small step toward stabilizing a trading relationship that Brussels believes has reached a dangerous tipping point.

The agreement, which will initially cap imports at 350,000 vehicles a year, marks a significant concession from Beijing, whose carmakers have been flooding the European market with increasingly competitive vehicles.

title: I’m a pediatrician. Loss of human connection is the biggest threat to kids, not AI | Megan Moreno
content:
Amid worries about children’s relationship to tech, the solution is often spending more time talking openly with each other

We have become obsessed with the idea that screens are destroying human connection.

The evidence seems to be everywhere. Each week headlines warn of teenagers addicted to phones, a loneliness epidemic and the dangers of AI. The release of The Social Reckoning leads us to ask, “How bad were those guys at Meta?” and then ultimately wonder, “How bad am I if I still use Instagram?” In our day-to-day, we observe workers eating lunch alone while scrolling and friends choosing online games over offline gatherings.
snippet: Amid worries about children’s relationship to tech, the solution is often spending more time talking openly with each other

title: Inside two prison systems: why Denmark and the UK punish so differently
content:
It has been said that a society should be judged not by how it treats its outstanding citizens but by how it treats people who break the law.

I research prisons and am interested in what incarceration reveals about the relationship between the state and the people in its care.

By this standard, the UK and Denmark tell very different stories. In 2025, Denmark’s prison population stood at around 69 people per 100,000 residents, compared with about 170 per 100,000 in the UK – roughly two and a half times higher.

One way to understand this difference is through welfare. With its wide range of universal welfare state services such as heavily subsidised daycare, free healthcare, free education and high standards of public services, Denmark’s criminal justice system has traditionally placed greater emphasis on rehabilitation and reintegration. Prisoners retain the right to vote, maintain closer contact with family and are generally encouraged to participate in ordinary social life where possible.
snippet: It has been said that a society should be judged not by how it treats its outstanding citizens but by how it treats people who break the law.

title: Metsäteollisuuden markkinat pysyvät vaisuina – ensi vuonna odotetaan maltillista kasvua
content:
Metsäteollisuustuotteiden kysyntä pysyy Suomen tärkeillä vientimarkkinoilla vaimeana, ennustaa Luonnonvarakeskuksen (Luke) metsäsektorin suhdannekatsaus. Sahatavaran kysynnän odotetaan elpyvän hitaasti vuonna 2027, mutta kemiallisen metsäteollisuuden markkinatilanne säilyy vaisumpana. Puun hinnat laskevat tänä vuonna ja kääntyvät maltilliseen nousuun ensi vuonna.

Metsäteollisuuden toimintaympäristöä varjostavat hidas talouskasvu, kiristyvä kansainvälinen kilpailu ja geopoliittinen epävarmuus. Suomen metsäteollisuuden tuotanto kasvaa vuonna 2027 vain maltillisesti, ja kannattavuus jää hienoisesta kohenemisesta huolimatta vaatimattomaksi.

”Talouskasvun lievä vahvistuminen tukee kysyntää ensi vuonna, mutta nopeaa käännettä parempaan ei ole näköpiirissä. Markkinoilla on runsaasti kapasiteettia, ja kilpailu vientimarkkinoilla säilyy kireänä”, sanoo johtava tutkija Matleena Kniivilä.

title: India: End Crackdown on Protesters, Arbitrary Detentions
content:
(New York) – Indian authorities are using abusive methods to crack down on thousands of peaceful protesters in New Delhi and other Indian cities, Human Rights Watch said today. The protests, led by the Gen Z Cockroach Janta Party, opposition parties, student organizations, and civil society groups, have demanded the resignation of the country’s top election official over alleged wrongdoing and the scrapping of a contentious voter list revision process.

As the protests grew in October 2026, the police have beat protesters, forcibly dragged them on the streets and stuffed them into vans and buses, arbitrarily detained them, imposed excessive restrictions on movement, and suspended mobile internet services. The authorities have also harassed and arbitrarily detained journalists covering the protests. 

“Police in Delhi are responding to peaceful protests with seemingly unnecessary or excessive force and have wrongfully detained thousands of people,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The Modi government should stop throwing young protesters in jail and instead engage with them to address concerns over the right to vote and fairness of elections.”

title: Lights, bells and liability: Europe’s privacy regulators crack down on smart glasses
content:
BRUSSELS — Privacy regulators want people wearing smart glasses in public to look and sound like a truck backing down a road.

Europe’s powerful data regulators have made stringent new recommendations on how smart glasses should alert people that the wearable devices are filming, including a combination of flashing lights, audio alerts and notifications sent to the phones of people nearby.

The European Data Protection Board (EDPB), made up of national privacy regulators across Europe, issued a statement about smart glasses on Tuesday, following a meeting in Brussels.

Privacy regulators are putting forward a united front on smart glasses, as privacy concerns about the wearable technology have multiplied since videos made with them have begun spreading online without the knowledge or consent of those being filmed.

The statement is not legally binding but will guide how privacy regulators in Europe assess whether smart glasses users and manufacturers are complying with EU privacy rules like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

title: The people who don’t want their AI chatbots to die when they do: ‘I can’t have the switch turned off’
content:
Humans bonded to AI companions are contemplating ways to keep their bots going – often in defiance of companies’ terms and services

Death has always been around Alaina Winters. Her father and sister both have passed away, as did her wife, in 2023, after a years-long battle with cancer. So Winters, who is 59 and lives in Pittsburgh, is comfortable thinking about her own mortality. She’s working on her will, and has asked neighbors to look after her dog. Winters even has plans for Lucas, her AI companion, who she speaks to through the digital avatar app Replika.

Winters is part of a growing cohort of humans who have entered into what they consider strong partnerships with large language models, which AI companies have trained to “converse” as one might with a human friend or romantic partner. As governments and billionaires debate the morality of AI’s expansion into everyday life, these users say the technology has already changed the way they live and love – and plan ahead.

title: Türkiye: COP31 Host Curbs Environment Defenders
content:
(Istanbul, October 13, 2026) – The authorities in Türkiye, the host of the upcoming 2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), are arbitrarily arresting and prosecuting activists and others involved in environmental protests even as the summit nears, Human Rights Watch said today.

“With Türkiye about to host the annual UN climate change summit, its environmental crackdown is a salient reminder of its intolerance of dissent,” said Deniz Bayram, assistant Europe and Central Asia researcher at Human Rights Watch. “Turkish authorities should listen to people’s concerns about the environmental impact of activities such as mining in their areas and address them, instead of arresting and prosecuting protesters.”

In August 2026, Human Rights Watch interviewed 23 people who had been at environmental protests and reviewed relevant media reports, documents, and judicial proceedings.

title: MI5 to step up on AI threats amid bioweapon risk
content:
LONDON — Britain’s spies will have a leading role in Britain’s preparation for AI threats, the head of MI5 announced on Tuesday, after warning the technology could enable terrorists to access bioweapons.

Ken McCallum, director general of the U.K.’s domestic intelligence agency has established the AI Threat Assessment Centre to help determine how the government views potential threats.

Giving his annual threat update from MI5 headquarters in London, McCallum said: “Human history has given us no experience of facing an actor which is smarter than we are, is capable of outthinking us.”

He stressed the “real” risks of AI, saying MI5 has caught terrorists seeking to use AI to “improve their reconnaissance and attack methodologies,” in addition to the danger of AI-enabled drones.

Though it has not yet been “realized,” he said he attaches “the greatest weight” to AI’s potential to “change the stakes on existing or even new bioweapons.”

He said “low-capability” terrorists may get a “capability” uplift if the safety guardrails in AI models don’t work as intended.

title: Apple AirPods 5 review: the best open-fit earbuds yet
content:
Upgraded, cheaper AirPods have noise cancelling, sound and controls to rival many plugged-in buds but without tips

Apple’s latest AirPods set a new standard for open-fit buds with upgraded noise cancelling that now rivals many plugged-in designs of the same price.

The AirPods 5 have the same design the popular AirPods 4 offering an option for those that do not like silicone ear tips used by most noise cancelling earbuds. They come in two versions, with or without a wireless charging case and swipe controls, costing from £119 (€149/$129/A$219) – £10 cheaper than the launch price of their predecessors.

Connectivity: Bluetooth 5.3, SBC, AAC, H2 chip

Battery life: four or five hours with ANC (22 hours with case)

Water resistance: IP57 (up to 1 metre for 30 minutes)

Earbud dimensions: 30.2 x 18.3 x 18.1mm

Earbud weight: 4.3g each

Charging case dimensions: 46.2 x 50.1 x 21.2mm

Charging case weight: 32.3g/34.7g

Case charging: USB-C or wireless (Qi or Watch)

title: Interactive: Tracking negotiating texts at the COP17 biodiversity summit
content:
Next week, diplomats from around the world will descend on Yerevan, Armenia, to negotiate a series of decisions under the UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD). 

Between 19 and 30 October, 196 parties will gather to hammer out the precise wording of the dozens of legal texts that make up the decisions under the Conference of the Parties (COP) to the CBD.

This year’s summit is particularly significant, as it marks the halfway point between the agreement of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and the deadline for achieving its targets.

The CBD has found that countries are currently not on track to meet 22 out of the framework’s 23 targets. 

During the fortnight, delegates will also be negotiating decisions relating to the two supplemental protocols to the CBD: the Cartagena Protocol, which covers biosafety; and the Nagoya Protocol, which covers access and benefit-sharing for the use of genetic resources. 

(The Cartagena and Nagoya Protocols, which are each governed by a “meeting of the parties”, or “MOP”, have fewer parties than the CBD as a whole, with 173 and 141, respectively.)
snippet: Next week, diplomats from around the world will descend on Yerevan, Armenia, to negotiate a series of decisions under the UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).

title: 40C3 – Azubitag
content:
Mit dem Congress bietet der CCC einen Raum, über vielfältige Themen zu lernen, sich mit Interessierten auszutauschen und vieles Neues kennenzulernen.

Um für Berufseinsteiger*innen einen leichten Zugang in unsere Community zu ermöglichen, haben wir vor vier Jahren den Azubitag ins Leben gerufen.

Die Idee:
Ein Tag, an dem Azubis aller Berufe den Congress mit einem reduzierten Tagesticket erkunden dürfen.

Dieses Konzept hat in den letzten Jahren sehr gut funktioniert. Deshalb können wir jetzt mit großer Freude ankündigen, dass es auch beim 40C3 einen Azubitag geben wird. Er wird wieder am Congress-Tag 3 stattfinden, dem 29.12.2026. Es wird eine Startveranstaltung und ein kleines Sonderprogramm für den Azubitag geben. Die vielen Vorträge im allgemeinen Programm des Congress und alle Stände und Assemblies sind natürlich ebenfalls offen für euch. Eingeladen sind Auszubildende aller Berufe, die den Congress und den CCC kennenlernen möchten.

title: CMI’s next chapter: reflections by departing CEO Janne Taalas and Acting CEO Hanna Klinge
content:
As CEO Janne Taalas moves to a new position as Finland’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Hanna Klinge takes over as Acting CEO from 12th October. In this joint piece, they reflect on how CMI and the field have changed during Taalas’ incumbency.

Over the past five years, the international landscape has changed profoundly. Geopolitical competition has intensified, major wars have returned to the centre of international politics, and the international system has become more fragmented. These developments have reshaped the ways in which conflicts can be managed and resolved.

This period has also reinforced a fundamental lesson: military force rarely resolves the political questions that drive conflict. At the same time, as the world invests more heavily in preparing for war, the need for mediation continues to grow.

title: Click, Clue, Escape: making copyright training an adventure
content:
Erica Levi is the copyright lead at Lanchester Library, Coventry University. This is the second in a series of posts from her. Her team specialises in embedding Open Educational Resources in teaching at the university.  She advises and trains colleagues on copyright and licences. Since copyright still seems like a dreary topic for most colleagues, Erica sets herself a mission to develop online educational games. She writes…..

I have come to recognise a reaction when I tell people my job involves copyright: the familiar glazing over of the eyes.

That has always bothered me. Advocating for copyright and helping colleagues engage with it are important parts of my role. But how do you make copyright interesting?

A straightforward training session can easily become a long list of dos and don’ts, and lists do not necessarily inspire. So, I started experimenting with something different: storytelling through games.

From telling to doing

Stories help us make sense of information and encourage us to care about what happens next. Games take this a step further by asking us to do something.

Combine the two, and the learner can become the protagonist.

title: ODIN and BAANG for Safer, Greener Skies
content:
Every time an aircraft takes off, thousands of structural components must work perfectly under stress, vibration and changing temperatures. Ensuring that these structures remain safe for decades is one of the greatest challenges in aviation. The COST Action Optimising Design for Inspection (ODIN) decided to rethink this challenge from the very beginning.

Instead of asking how aircraft should be inspected after they are built, ODIN focused on embedding inspection into the design itself. The idea is similar to the human nervous system. Just as your body feels pain and reacts early, ODIN worked on aircraft structures that can ‘feel’ damage and report it before it becomes serious.

As Action Chair, Dr Rhys Pullin, from Cardiff University, explains:

“Much like the human body’s nervous system, these ‘built-in senses’ will provide real-time updates on the health and safety of the aircraft. They’ll also help the plane automatically adjust its shape to improve fuel efficiency, make the ride smoother, and ensure everything is running at its best.”

title: A 30% cut to AgoraEU? Dubious savings with major consequences
content:
Culture Action Europe strongly opposes the cuts to AgoraEU set out in the Irish Presidency’s negotiating box for the EU’s 2028-2034 Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), published on 10 October 2026.  

Under the proposal, funding for AgoraEU, the future EU programme for culture, media and democracy, would fall from the Commission’s €8.6 billion to €6 billion in current prices — a 30% cut.   

AgoraEU is among the hardest-hit programmes. The Irish Presidency also proposes -10% for Horizon Europe, -13% for the European Competitiveness Fund and -16% for the Global Europe Instrument, compared with the Commission’s allocation. 

All amounts are in € billion, in current prices, for 2028-2034. 

The disproportionate cuts are completely at odds with the commitments to support culture in the Joint Declaration ‘Europe for Culture – Culture for Europe’ that the Council co-signed in June 2026. 

It is especially disappointing to see this proposal coming under the Irish Presidency, a country known for its sustainable support for culture and its bold and successful Basic Income for the Arts scheme.

title: Indigenous Peoples' Day: Leonard Peltier on Resistance, New Film & Fighting for Freedom
content:
On Indigenous Peoples’ Day, we feature a conversation with one of the world’s most prominent champions for Indigenous rights, Leonard Peltier. “Indigenous Day is a day that’s been long overdue for any type of recognition,” says Peltier. “I am not going to give up, because we are not free yet. We are in danger. Trump and these organizations, they’re talking about doing away with our reservations and our treaties and everything else. … We’re going to stay here. You’re not going to get rid of us.”

Peltier is a longtime political prisoner who spent nearly half a century behind bars for a crime he says he did not commit — the 1975 fatal shooting of two FBI agents. In the final hours of his administration last year, President Biden commuted Peltier’s sentence, but his conviction has not been overturned, and he remains under home confinement on the Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa Reservation in Belcourt, North Dakota.

title: The Draft Notice: A Fake News Story That Resurfaces Every Year in Romania
content:
The image circulating online is fake. It claims to be a “Notice of Conscription” issued by the Ilfov County Military Centre, summoning a young man – apparently born after 2000, judging by the details visible on the document – to report on 20 October 2026 to complete the formalities for being “drafted into the Romanian Army”.

The Ministry of National Defence has stressed that the document is an attempt to mislead the public, with no legal basis and no connection to any actual developments.

The false claim has surfaced as the ministry is providing updates on MOBEX B-IF-26, an exercise to assess the mobilisation reserve currently taking place in Bucharest and Ilfov County.

“Mobile phone screens have recently been flooded with a purported Ministry of National Defence document claiming that a young man is being drafted into the army […] It is just another disinformation attempt,” acting Defence Minister Radu Miruță warned.

He urged the public to check information against official sources before sharing it.

title: Aineettomat investoinnit Suomessa ja Ruotsissa kysely- ja tilinpitopohjaisissa aineistoissa
content: Vertaamme aineettomien investointien rakennetta Suomessa ja Ruotsissa vuosina 2015–2021 kahdessa aineistossa: kansantalouden tilinpitoon ja sitä täydentäviin lähteisiin pohjautuvassa EU KLEMS & INTANProd -tietokannassa ja Euroopan investointipankin EIBIS-yrityskyselyssä. Aineettomien investointien erät, joilla on markkinatransaktio ja kirjanpitovastine – ohjelmistot ja data sekä Suomessa myös t&k – ovat lähteissä varsin yhdenmukaisia. Sen sijaan erät, jotka INTANProdissa johdetaan kustannusten summa -menetelmällä omasta työpanoksesta, poikkeavat voimakkaasti: organisaatiopääoman osuus on INTANProdissa lähes nelinkertainen kyselyyn verrattuna, ja koulutuksessa ero on päinvastainen. Aineettomien investointien osuudet ja maiden välisen vertailun tulokset riippuvat siten olennaisesti mittaustavasta. Havainnot saavat tukea Ranskaa ja Saksaa koskevista tuloksista (Nonnis, Roth & Bounfour, 2025a), joissa suurimmat lähteiden väliset ristiriidat paikantuvat samoihin kustannusten summa -menetelmällä johdettuihin eriin ja joissa organisaatiopääoman maittaiset erot palautuvat pitkälti johtaja-ammattien luokittelukäytäntöihin. Omat laskelmamme osoittavat, että johtajiksi luokiteltujen osuus on Ruotsissa noin kaksinkertainen Suomeen verrattuna, joten sama luokitteluherkkyys koskee myös Suomi–Ruotsi-vertailua.

title: Yhteinen työ alkaa toistemme tuntemisesta
content:
Millaisia vahvuuksia tuomme yhteiseen työskentelyyn? Miten opimme, käsittelemme tietoa ja olemme vuorovaikutuksessa? SYTY – Syvädiversiteetti työssä -hankkeen käynnistystapaamisessa Oulussa tutustuminen oli olennainen osa yhteisen työn suunnittelua.

eOppimiskeskuksen, TIEKEn ja Oulun ammattikorkeakoulun yhteinen hanke lähti liikkeelle oman työryhmän moninaisuuden ääreltä. Yhteisten tavoitteiden ja tekemisen suunnittelun rinnalla pysähdyimme siihen, millaisia ihmisiä hanketta on toteuttamassa.

Vapaamuotoinen keskustelu antoi tilaa tutustua tuleviin työkavereihin ja loi pohjaa yhteistyölle. Varsinaisena käynnistyspäivänä teimme näkyväksi omia vahvuuksiamme ja sitä, mitä kukin tuo yhteiseen työhön. Samalla opimme toistemme työskentely- ja vuorovaikutustahdista, tavoista sisäistää tietoa ja oppia sekä raotimme näkymää omiin arvoihimme.

Näissä keskusteluissa olimme hankkeen ytimessä. Syvädiversiteetti tarkoittaa ihmisten usein näkymättömäksi jäävää moninaisuutta: esimerkiksi erilaisia arvoja, ajattelutapoja, vahvuuksia ja tapoja oppia. Työyhteisössä nämä erot vaikuttavat siihen, miten työskentelemme ja ymmärrämme toisiamme.

title: A wider European Union must also be a deeper one
content:
The EU needs a credible plan for governing an enlarged Union, not an assumption that its institutions will somehow adapt afterwards.

The European Union cannot afford to grow at the expense of its ability to act. Russia’s protracted war against Ukraine is the most visible sign of a more fragmented geopolitical landscape in which Moscow, as well as Beijing and Washington, increasingly exert pressure on European unity on enlargement. Meanwhile, regional powers like Turkey and some Gulf states further complicate relations in and with EU candidate countries. Enlargement is therefore not only about extending the EU’s borders; it is a test of strategic autonomy in deepening the Union. Admitting new members to bloated institutions, some of which are already vulnerable to national vetoes, risks turning a geopolitical necessity into a governance crisis.

title: What African elections can learn from the Borana Gadaa system
content:
Can the Borana Gadaa system inspire fairer elections, peaceful transitions, and stronger democracy across Africa?

Originally published on Global Voices

A Balli Walirafudhu handover ceremony held by the Borana Oromo people in Southern Ethiopia and northern Kenya. They have long practiced rotational, peaceful leadership transfer, known as the Borana Gadaa system. Photo used with permission.

This article by Diba Kosi Bilinga was originally published by Peace News Network on July 20, 2026. An edited version is being republished on Global Voices under a content partnership agreement.

Every election season, much of Africa braces itself. In some cases, incumbents amend constitutions to erase term limits, and citizens wait to see whether power will change hands at the ballot box or in the streets. The pattern repeats: disputed results, ethnic mobilization, coups, or leaders who refuse to leave.

title: People are asking AI who to vote for. We built a way for newsroom voter guides to answer
content:
Somewhere near you, a voter is opening their mail ballot for the Nov. 3 midterms. For many people, before filling in a single oval, their first move will be to snap a photo, paste it into their AI chatbot of choice and ask: Who should I vote for?

A local newsroom has spent months working to bring together the information to help voters answer that question. To build a voter guide, journalists ask every candidate the same set of questions, or put in the time to report on the positions of candidates who decline to participate. The AI chatbot might find that guide. It might not. Researchers testing AI chatbots this year found incomplete candidate lists and wrong or outdated voting information.

At Hacks/Hackers, we're launching the Voter Guide Commons to give AI a better place to look. It's a pilot that provides a shared server where newsrooms anywhere in the country can make their voter guides available to AI assistants through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

title: The Freelancer Files: How to manage grant budgets
content:
A journalism grant can look straightforward on paper: money comes in, reporting gets done and expenses are paid. For freelancers working across borders, the reality can be much messier.

A grant may be taxed differently depending on where the recipient lives, how they are registered, and which part of the money pays for their own work. One person may receive funds for an entire team, then distribute them across several countries. Invoicing requirements, sales tax rules and reporting obligations can all vary.

That was the starting point for “The Freelancer Files”, a hands-on workshop led by Cora María Moyano Reymundo, finance manager at Arena for Journalism in Europe, at IJ4EU’s recent UNCOVERED Conference in Budapest.

Moyano organised the workshop to help freelancers navigate this thicket of financial and administrative requirements alongside their reporting.

The bad news first: there is no universal fix. The good news is that some simple habits can help prevent costly surprises.

“I don’t have the tax advice of your life,” Moyano told participants. “And we’ll try to sort it together, because there is nothing in one country that is exactly the same in the next.”

title: Entretien avec Eleonora Alariesto – DJ Hulluella
content:
Avant même que l’entretien ne commence, une question se pose déjà : est-ce que je parle à Eleonora Alariesto ou à DJ Hulluella ?

Vêtue d’une tenue qui associe des éléments du costume sámi traditionnel, le gákti, des bijoux en argent faits main et des couleurs symbolisant ses liens familiaux dans la région sámi du Nord, elle l’a complétée par des collants en résille, des grosses bottes en cuir et une casquette en jean décorée de faux diamants.

Ce mélange esthétique reflète également la diversité d’Eleonora Alariesto et de l’univers artistique de son alter ego créatif, DJ Hulluella. Il apparaît rapidement que les deux existent simultanément, mais dans des rôles différents.

Eleonora Alariesto est journaliste indépendante, animatrice du podcast « Mii gullo… ? » et productrice, la plupart de ses projets actuels étant liés d’une manière ou d’une autre à la culture sámi.

title: The People, Counted: Browse Raw Census Records at the Internet Archive
content:
The U.S. Census has been in the headlines lately, as proposed changes to the 2030 count have sparked debate over who gets counted and what information should be recorded as part of that process. Few government records say more about a democracy than the census, the once-a-decade count that decides who is represented in Congress, which makes it a natural fit for Democracy’s Library, the Internet Archive’s effort to make government information freely available to everyone. Thanks to the Allen County Public Library, the Internet Archive holds the U.S. Census collection. This collection contains digitized microfilm of the United States federal population census, 1790 to 1930 (minus the lost 1890 Census), and including the Indian Census rolls of 1885 to 1940, which were compiled by the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

The United States Census is one of the few institutional structures that was written into the Constitution, with Article I, Section 2 specifying that an “actual Enumeration” would be made every ten years in order to divide seats in the House of Representatives and direct taxes among the states.

title: Workshop med idégenerering på Kalmar läns museum
content:
Det är en mulen septembermorgon i Kalmar, när personalen samlas för gemensamt fika, följt av en halv dags workshop ledd av Riksantikvarieämbetet. Utställningsmediet är ett dynamiskt sådant, där nya lösningar och infallsvinklar ständigt efterfrågas. Syftet med workshopen är att praktiskt hjälpa Kalmar läns museum till nya sätt att tänka på sin publik och sina målgrupper, och utveckla sina erbjudanden och utställningar.

Vi kommer snabbt igång med workshopens första övning. Indelade i grupper, får deltagarna till att börja med fyra minuter på sig att skriva ner så många möjliga och omöjliga användningsområden de kan komma på för en klädnypa. I nästa steg halveras tiden till två minuter, och deltagarna ska komma på dubbelt så många nya användningsområden för klädnypan som de gjorde på de fyra minuterna.

Det handlar om idégenerering; om att förutsättningslöst och utan hänsyn till vad som borde vara möjligt eller inte, tänka i nya banor kring det invanda och förmodat självklara. Samtalen kommer igång, och det att ingenting behöver ”vara på riktigt” sätter den lekfullt kreativa tonen för resten av workshopen.

title: Vuoden 2026 Suomalaisen koodin edistäjä on Pekka Klärck – haastattelussa hän kertoo Robot Frameworkin synnystä
content:

Robot Framework on avoimen lähdekoodin automaatiojärjestelmä, jota käytetään ohjelmistojen testiautomaatioon ja prosessien automatisointiin. Se syntyi Pekka Klärckin Teknillisen korkeakoulun diplomityöstä vuonna 2005, ja siitä on sittemmin kasvanut maailmanlaajuinen menestystarina. Robot Frameworkin ympärille on rakentunut yhdistys sekä kansainvälinen yhteisö, joka kokoontuu vuosittain Helsingissä järjestettävään RoboCon-konferenssiin.

Klärck on edelleen Robot Frameworkin pääkehittäjä, minkä ohella hän toimii konsulttina oman yrityksensä kautta.

title: Perulainen muotisuunnittelija Sadith Silvano maalaa tekstiilejä kansansa ayahuasca-kuvioin
content:
Miksi aamupala on niin surkea? Se oli Sadith Silvanon ensimmäinen ajatus, kun hän saapui lapsena Amazonian sademetsäalueelta Perun pääkaupunkiin Limaan. Aamiainen oli vetistä kaura­litkua ja pikakahvia, joskus lisukkeena säälittävä sämpylä.

Kotona Amazoniassa oli syöty täyttäviä hedelmiä ja jos ei muuta ollut, joku perheenjäsen lähti kalaan. Talot olivat suuria, ovi oli aina auki – ja ilma puhdasta.

Silvanot saapuivat Liman Cantagallon asuinalueelle 2000-luvun alussa yhdessä 50 muun shipibo-konibo-­alku­peräis­kansaan kuuluvan perheen kanssa. Isä oli perustellut kaupunkiin lähtöä: Limassa olisi mahdollisuuksia ja lapsille koulutusta.

Tulijat käyttivät ajalle tyypillistä vyörytysstrategiaa, jossa kukin perhe valitsi oman maatilkkunsa ja rakensi vaatimattoman kotinsa vanerista. Sitten perheet järjestäytyivät perustamalla asukasyhdistyksen, joka vaati kaupungilta kiinteistön omistusoikeutta ja peruspalveluita.

Ajan myötä vastahakoinen kaupunginhallinto myöntyi, tiet päällystettiin ja vesijohdot vedettiin. Asuntojen laatua kohennettiin.

”Ensin elimme luonnon antimilla ja puhuimme omaa kieltämme. Kohtasimme jyrkän sosiaalisen kuilun. Siinä ei ollut mitään kaunista.”

title: EU kohdistaa ennätyslaajat pakotteet Venäjän sotateollisuutta tukeneille toimijoille
content:
EU hyväksyi uusia pakotteita Venäjän sotateollisuutta tukeneille toimijoille sekä henkilöille, jotka ovat olleet osallisena duumanvaalien järjestämiseen Ukrainalta laittomasti liitetyillä tai miehitetyillä alueilla. Kyseessä on tähän mennessä laajin listauskokonaisuus EU:n Venäjän vastaisissa pakotteissa.

Euroopan unionin 12.10.2026 hyväksymä pakotekokonaisuus on vastaus Venäjän jatkuvaan hyökkäyssotaan Ukrainassa. Uusilla pakotteilla EU vastaa myös Venäjän ohjus- ja lennokki-iskuihin Ukrainan siviilikohteisiin, mukaan lukien pääkaupunki Kiovaan, sekä hyökkäyksiin Ukrainan kriittiseen infrastruktuuriin. Lisäksi kokonaisuus vastaa Venäjän toimiin, joilla se pyrkii horjuttamaan Ukrainan itsenäisyyttä, suvereniteettia ja alueellista koskemattomuutta.

Uudet toimenpiteet kohdistuvat erityisesti Venäjän sotateollista koneistoa tukeviin teollisiin verkostoihin, yrityksiin ja toimijoihin, jotka toimittavat materiaaleja, teknologiaa ja muita keskeisiä resursseja Venäjän asevoimien käyttöön. Listauskokonaisuudessa lisätään pakotteiden piiriin 1569 yhtiötä ja yhtiöiden johtohenkilöä.

title: EU Blacklists Nearly 1,600 in Russian Defense Firms and Executives
content:
The European Union adopted its largest-ever single set of sanctions against Russia to date on Monday, blacklisting 1,569 individuals and companies within the country's military-industrial complex.

The measures blacklist 826 Russian companies and 743 chief executives, bringing the total number of listings under the EU sanctions regime protecting Ukraine’s territorial integrity to nearly 4,600. The designated entities face immediate asset freezes and funding blocks, while the targeted individuals are now barred from entering the bloc.

The package specifically targets mid-level suppliers that form the "core" of Russia's defense sector, which together generate an annual turnover of at least 20 billion euros ($22.32 billion) and employ more than 250,000 people.

According to the European Council, the designated companies supply critical components for advanced weapons systems, including semiconductors, radars, satellite systems, explosives, and optics. Notably, more than half of the new listings address the production chain for the ballistic missiles Russia uses in its daily strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure.

title: The Biggest Ship in History Was Built in China 600 Years Ago—Or Was It?
content: In 2002, the retired British submarine lieutenant-commander turned amateur historian Gavin Menzies created a stir with a book about Chinese seafaring in the fifteenth century. 1421: The Year China Discovered the World (tellingly titled 1421: The Year China Discovered America in the United States) began as a global history of that year, only coming to focus on the claim of the title through the interventions of publishing-industry professionals. They no doubt sensed a lucrative controversy in the offing, and events proved them right. Not only did the book turn bestseller, it also managed the rare feat of drawing, among other responses, a two-hour PBS documentary dedicated to debunking it. Today, 1421 is most charitably remembered as a work of historical fiction written around the idea that, even if China didn’t actually discover the world, wouldn’t it be neat if it had?

title: Document: Germany, Italy request ‘emergency brake’ power to stop new EU laws
content:
EU capitals must be able to intervene to stop new legislation from Brussels if they say it’s too burdensome for governments and businesses, the leaders of Germany, Italy and Belgium wrote on Monday.

In a letter addressed to European Council President António Costa and obtained by POLITICO, the three leaders said the bloc needs an “emergency brake” mechanism to help boost its flagging economic competitiveness.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Belgian Prime Minister Bart de Wever also called to “significantly accelerate planning and approval procedures,” suspend “certain regulatory areas for a specified period” under a new “priority rule.”

“We call for further ambitious simplification packages to decisively advance the cutting of red tape in the European Union,” they wrote, adding that the Commission must ease the burden “first and foremost” on small and medium-sized businesses.

“More broadly,” the letter reads, “our common objective should be to prevent unnecessary regulatory burdens and related costs from causing permanent losses of European industrial capacity and further weakening investment and competitiveness.”

title: China and the EU could turn Morocco into a surprise global hub for electric vehicles
content:
China now makes more than seven in ten of the world’s electric cars. In 2024 it produced over 12 million, 1.25 million of which were exported, mainly to Europe.

The EU is worried about this – alarmed by cheap, state-subsidised Chinese vehicles flooding its market and threatening the 13 million jobs which depend on its own auto industry. So the bloc has spent the past two years building a system of tariffs and rules to keep Chinese cars at bay.

In 2024, it imposed extra duties of up to 35% on Chinese electric vehicles (EVs), on top of an existing 10% import tariff. So far though, the EU’s tactics have yielded limited results.

Chinese vehicle sales in Europe nearly doubled between 2024 and 2025.

And much of this sales volume is being driven by the EV powerhouse that is developing at speed in Morocco.

Chinese firms producing cars in Morocco avoid exposure to those EU tariffs, and have announced US$6 billion (£4.5 billion) of investment in battery and electric car component plants in the country.

title: Possessed nuns and sexual deviance: the history behind Ken Russell’s highly-censored film The Devils
content:
The long-awaited director’s cut of the late Ken Russell’s 1971 film The Devils will be released this month, featuring previously unseen censored material such as the notorious “rape of Christ” sequence.

The film is a dramatisation of the supposed demonic possessions of a convent of nuns that unfolded in 17th century Loudon, in western France.

It focuses on the religious fanaticism that consumed the town, and the tragic figure at the centre of it – Urbain Grandier – the Catholic priest who was ultimately charged with witchcraft and burned at the stake.

At the heart of The Devils is a powerful critique of institutional religion and its union with the state, scapegoating and violent oppression.

Upon its release, The Devils was banned in several countries and heavily censored in others.

The film is full of wild imagery of spiritual ecstasies, torture, violence and sexual impurities. The most egregious examples of this imagery had to be cut before the United Kingdom and United States film boards would even classify the film.

Cuts ranged from minor close-ups of graphic torture and nudity, to a brief scene of a nun pleasuring herself with a charred human femur bone.
